title.zh: 卷二十六 魏書二十六 滿田牽郭傳
title.en: Volume 26: Book of Wei 26 - Biographies of Man, Tian, Qian, and Guo
title.raw: 卷二十六 魏書二十六 滿田牽郭傳 Volume 26: Book of Wei 26 - Biographies of Man, Tian, Qian, and Guo

sentences.zh: 滿寵 田豫 牽招 郭淮

translations.literal: Man Chong; Tian Yu; Qian Zhao; Guo Huai
translations.idiomatic: Man Chong, Tian Yu, Qian Zhao, and Guo Huai.

sentences.zh: 滿寵字伯寧，山陽昌邑人也。

translations.literal: Man Chong's courtesy name was Boning; he was a man of Changyi in Shanyang.
translations.idiomatic: Man Chong, courtesy name Boning, was a native of Changyi in Shanyang.

sentences.zh: 年十八，爲郡督郵。

translations.literal: At age eighteen he became the commandery courier inspector (duyou).
translations.idiomatic: At eighteen he was appointed courier inspector for the commandery.

sentences.zh: 時郡內李朔等各擁部曲，害于平民，太守使寵糾焉。

translations.literal: At that time Li Shuo and others in the commandery each maintained personal followings and harmed the common people; the grand administrator ordered Chong to investigate them.
translations.idiomatic: Li Shuo and others in the commandery then commanded private followings and preyed on civilians; the grand administrator sent Chong to rein them in.

sentences.zh: 朔等請罪，不復鈔略。

translations.literal: Shuo and the others begged forgiveness and did not again raid and plunder.
translations.idiomatic: They sued for pardon and ceased their pillaging.

sentences.zh: 守高平令。

translations.literal: He served as magistrate of Gaoping.
translations.idiomatic: He held office as magistrate of Gaoping.

sentences.zh: 縣人張苞爲郡督郵，貪穢受取，干亂吏政。

translations.literal: A man of the county, Zhang Bao, held the post of commandery courier inspector; he was greedy and corrupt, accepting bribes and throwing the clerks' administration into disorder.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Bao of that county was the commandery courier inspector—venal, grasping, and meddling with official business.

sentences.zh: 寵因其來在傳舍，率吏卒出收之，詰責所犯，即日考竟，遂棄官歸。

translations.literal: When [Zhang Bao] arrived at the relay inn, Chong led clerks and soldiers out to seize him, interrogated him concerning his offenses, that same day brought the examination to its conclusion [with execution], then abandoned office and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Bao showed up at the post station, Chong marched clerks and soldiers out to arrest him, questioned him about his crimes, had the case resolved that same day, resigned his post, and went home.

sentences.zh: 太祖臨兖州，辟爲從事。

translations.literal: When the Founding Emperor [Cao Cao] came to Yan Province, [Chong] was summoned as an aide.
translations.idiomatic: After Cao Cao entered Yan Province, Chong received appointment as an aide.

sentences.zh: 及爲大將軍，辟署西曹屬，爲許令。

translations.literal: When [Cao Cao] became grand general, [Chong] was appointed to the western bureau staff and served as magistrate of Xu.
translations.idiomatic: Once Cao Cao took the title of grand general, Chong joined the western bureau staff and became magistrate of Xu.

sentences.zh: 時曹洪宗室親貴，有賔客在界，數犯法，寵收治之。

translations.literal: At that time Cao Hong, being of the imperial clan and honored as kin, had retainers within the jurisdiction who repeatedly violated the law; Chong arrested and prosecuted them.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Hong, a proud kinsman of the ruling house, kept guests in the district who broke the law again and again; Chong took them into custody.

sentences.zh: 洪書報寵，寵不聽。

translations.literal: Hong wrote to Chong; Chong would not heed him.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Hong wrote to intercede; Chong refused to listen.

sentences.zh: 洪白太祖，太祖召許主者。

translations.literal: Hong reported to the Founding Emperor, and the Founding Emperor summoned the Xu official in charge.
translations.idiomatic: Hong appealed to Cao Cao, who called in the chief clerk responsible for Xu.

sentences.zh: 寵知將欲原，乃速殺之。

translations.literal: Chong knew that [the emperor] was about to grant a pardon, so he swiftly executed [the prisoner].
translations.idiomatic: Chong saw that a pardon was coming and put the man to death at once.

sentences.zh: 太祖喜曰：「當事不當耳邪？

translations.literal: [The Founding Emperor] rejoiced and said, 'One must handle affairs as they ought to be handled—is it not so?'
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao said with satisfaction, 'You did what the office required—was that not right?'

sentences.zh: 」故太尉楊彪收付縣獄，尚書令荀彧、少府孔融等並屬寵：「但當受辭，勿加考掠。

translations.literal: Therefore the former grand commandant Yang Biao was seized and handed over to the county prison; the minister over the masses Xun Yu, the chamberlain for the palace revenues Kong Rong, and others all instructed Chong: 'Only take his statement; do not apply torture.'
translations.idiomatic: The former grand commandant Yang Biao was jailed in the county; Xun Yu, Kong Rong, and others told Chong to record Yang's words only and skip the lash.

sentences.zh: 」寵一無所報，考訊如法。

translations.literal: Chong made no reply whatsoever and interrogated [Yang Biao] according to law.
translations.idiomatic: Chong ignored them and questioned Yang under the normal judicial procedure.

sentences.zh: 數日，求見太祖，言之曰：「楊彪考訊無他辭語。

translations.literal: After several days he requested an audience with the Founding Emperor and said to him, 'In examining Yang Biao there has been no other confession.'
translations.idiomatic: A few days later he sought an audience and reported, 'Under interrogation Yang Biao has admitted nothing further.'

sentences.zh: 當殺者宜先彰其罪；

translations.literal: Those who deserve execution ought first to make their crimes manifest;
translations.idiomatic: If a man must die, his guilt should be displayed first;

sentences.zh: 此人有名海內，若罪不明，必大失民望，竊爲明公惜之。

translations.literal: this man has a reputation throughout the realm; if his guilt is not clear, you will greatly lose the people's confidence—I privately regret this on Lord's behalf.
translations.idiomatic: his name is known across the empire—if his offense stays obscure the throne will forfeit public trust, and I fear that would wound your lordship.

sentences.zh: 」太祖即日赦出彪。

translations.literal: ' That same day the Founding Emperor issued an amnesty and released Biao.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao pardoned Yang Biao that very day.

sentences.zh: 初，彧、融聞考掠彪，皆怒，及因此得了，更善寵。

translations.literal: At first, when Yu and Rong heard that [Yang] Biao was being tortured, they were angry; when they therefore obtained this outcome, they esteemed Chong all the more.
translations.idiomatic: At first Xun Yu and Kong Rong were furious when they heard Yang was being beaten; once matters turned out as they did, they respected Chong more than ever.

sentences.zh: 〈臣松之以爲楊公積德之門，身爲名臣，縱有愆負，猶宜保祐，況淫刑所濫，而可加其楚掠乎？

translations.literal: <Your servant Songzhi considers that the house of Lord Yang was a gate piled high with accumulated virtue; [Yang Biao] himself was a renowned minister—even if there were faults to answer for, one ought still to shelter him; how much more when cruel punishments were wantonly applied—could one yet add birch strokes and flogging for him?
translations.idiomatic: 〈Pei Songzhi remarks: The Yangs were a household steeped in virtue; Yang Biao was an eminent minister—even had he owed some fault he deserved protection; all the more under indiscriminate cruelty could one justify laying on torture.

sentences.zh: 若理應考訊，荀、孔二賢豈其妄有相請屬哉？

translations.literal: If according to principle he ought to have been interrogated, could the two worthies Xun and Kong have vainly issued such entreaties?
translations.idiomatic: If legal questioning had truly been warranted, would Xun Yu and Kong Rong have pleaded with Chong for nothing?

sentences.zh: 寵以此爲能，酷吏之用心耳。

translations.literal: That Chong took this as ability was the mind-set of a harsh official.
translations.idiomatic: To pride oneself on such conduct is the logic of a cruel judge.

sentences.zh: 雖有後善，何解前虐？〉

translations.literal: Though there was later good conduct, how does it redeem earlier cruelty?>
translations.idiomatic: Later virtue cannot erase earlier brutality.〉

sentences.zh: 時袁紹盛於河朔，而汝南紹之本郡，門生賔客布在諸縣，擁兵拒守。

translations.literal: At that time Yuan Shao was powerful north of the Yellow River, while Runan was Shao's home commandery; disciples and retainers were spread through the counties, holding troops and refusing submission.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Shao dominated the Hebei plain, and Runan—his native commandery—teemed with his clients and partisans in every county, armed and defiant.

sentences.zh: 太祖憂之，以寵爲汝南太守。

translations.literal: The Founding Emperor worried over this and appointed Chong grand administrator of Runan.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao, troubled by the situation, named Chong administrator of Runan.

sentences.zh: 寵募其服從者五百人，率攻下二十餘壁，誘其未降渠帥，於坐上殺十餘人，一時皆平。

translations.literal: Chong recruited five hundred men who were willing to submit, led attacks that reduced more than twenty fortifications, enticed the band chiefs who had not yet surrendered, and at a banquet killed more than ten of them; in one stroke all was pacified.
translations.idiomatic: He enlisted five hundred willing men, stormed over twenty strongholds, lured leaders who still held out, slew more than ten of them at their seats, and thus pacified the region in one sweep.

sentences.zh: 得戶二萬，兵二千人，令就田業。

translations.literal: He obtained twenty thousand households and two thousand soldiers and ordered them to take up farming.
translations.idiomatic: He registered twenty thousand households and two thousand troops and set them to working the land.

sentences.zh: 建安十三年，從太祖征荊州。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year of Jian'an he accompanied the Founding Emperor on the campaign against Jing Province.
translations.idiomatic: In Jian'an 13 he joined Cao Cao's expedition against Jing Province.

sentences.zh: 大軍還，留寵行奮威將軍，屯當陽。

translations.literal: When the great army returned, [Cao Cao] left Chong acting general who Inspires Might and stationed him at Dangyang.
translations.idiomatic: On the army's return Chong stayed behind as acting Inspires Might general, camped at Dangyang.

sentences.zh: 孫權數擾東陲，復召寵還爲汝南太守，賜爵關內侯。

translations.literal: Sun Quan repeatedly harassed the eastern frontier; [Cao Cao] again summoned Chong back to be grand administrator of Runan and enfeoffed him as village marquis within the passes.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan kept raiding the east, so Chong was recalled to Runan and granted a secondary marquisate inside the passes.

sentences.zh: 關羽圍襄陽，寵助征南將軍曹仁屯樊城拒之，而左將軍于禁等軍以霖雨水長爲羽所沒。

translations.literal: When Guan Yu besieged Xiangyang, Chong assisted the south-conquering general Cao Ren, who was stationed at Fan city to resist him, while the general of the left Yu Jin and other forces were drowned by Guan Yu because the rains swelled the waters.
translations.idiomatic: With Guan Yu investing Xiangyang, Chong reinforced Cao Ren at Fan; Yu Jin and his hosts were swept away when floodwaters rose.

sentences.zh: 羽急攻樊城，樊城得水，往往崩壞，衆皆失色。

translations.literal: Guan Yu pressed the assault on Fan city; Fan city was inundated and its walls often crumbled; the troops all lost color.
translations.idiomatic: Guan Yu hammered Fan; water lapped the walls and sections fell; the defenders went pale.

sentences.zh: 或謂仁曰：「今日之危，非力所支。

translations.literal: Someone said to Ren, 'Today's peril cannot be sustained by strength.
translations.idiomatic: Some urged Ren, 'This crisis is beyond what force can bear.

sentences.zh: 可及羽圍未合，乘輕船夜走，雖失城，尚可全身。

translations.literal: Before Guan Yu's encirclement closes, take light boats and flee by night—though you lose the city, you may yet preserve your life.'
translations.idiomatic: Slip away in small boats under cover of night before the ring closes—you may surrender the city but save yourselves.'

sentences.zh: 」寵曰：「山水速疾，冀其不久。

translations.literal: ' Chong said, 'The mountain flood runs swiftly; I hope it will not last long.
translations.idiomatic: Chong replied, 'The flood is fierce but should ebb soon.

sentences.zh: 聞羽遣別將已在郟下，自許以南，百姓擾擾，羽所以不敢遂進者，恐吾軍掎其後耳。

translations.literal: I have heard that Guan Yu has detached another commander who is already below Jia; from Xu southward the common people are in turmoil; the reason Guan Yu does not dare advance straightway is that he fears our army will pinch him from the rear.
translations.idiomatic: Word is Guan Yu has sent a column toward Jia; south of Xu the people are in uproar; he hesitates to push south because he dreads a stab in the rear.

sentences.zh: 今若遁去，洪河以南，非復國家有也；

translations.literal: If we now flee, south of the great river will no longer belong to the state;
translations.idiomatic: If we bolt now, everything south of the river ceases to be ours;

sentences.zh: 君宜待之。

translations.literal: you ought to await developments.'
translations.idiomatic: wait it out.'

sentences.zh: 」仁曰：「善。

translations.literal: ' Ren said, 'Good.'
translations.idiomatic: Ren said, 'Well said.'

sentences.zh: 」寵乃沈白馬，與軍人盟誓。

translations.literal: ' Chong then drowned a white horse and swore an oath with the soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: Chong sacrificed a white horse and bound the garrison with an oath.

sentences.zh: 會徐晃等救至，寵力戰有功，羽遂退。

translations.literal: When Xu Huang's relief force arrived, Chong fought hard and distinguished himself, and Guan Yu then withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: When Xu Huang's reinforcements came, Chong fought stubbornly; Guan Yu pulled back.

sentences.zh: 進封安昌亭侯。

translations.literal: He was advanced to village marquis of Anchang.
translations.idiomatic: His fief was advanced to village marquis of Anchang.

sentences.zh: 文帝即王位，遷揚武將軍。

translations.literal: When the Emperor Wen assumed the rank of king, [Chong] was promoted to general who Displays Martial Might.
translations.idiomatic: Once Cao Pi took the kingship, Chong became general who Displays Martial Might.

sentences.zh: 破吳於江陵有功，更拜伏波將軍，屯新野。

translations.literal: He defeated Wu at Jiangling with merit and was further appointed general who Subdues the Waves, stationed at Xinye.
translations.idiomatic: He earned credit routing Wu at Jiangling, was named general who Subdues the Waves, and encamped at Xinye.

sentences.zh: 大軍南征，到精湖，寵帥諸軍在前，與賊隔水相對。

translations.literal: When the great army marched south and reached Jing Lake, Chong led the various armies in the van and faced the enemy across the water.
translations.idiomatic: On the southern expedition at Jing Lake he commanded the vanguard, confronting the foe across the channel.

sentences.zh: 寵勑諸將曰：「今夕風甚猛，賊必來燒軍，宜爲其備。

translations.literal: Chong ordered the generals, saying, 'The wind is violent tonight; the enemy is sure to come burn the camp—you ought to prepare for it.'
translations.idiomatic: He warned his officers, 'The gale tonight is fierce—the enemy will try to fire the camp; stand ready.'

sentences.zh: 」諸軍皆警。

translations.literal: All the troops were alert.
translations.idiomatic: Every unit went on alert.

sentences.zh: 夜半，賊果遣十部伏夜來燒，寵掩擊破之，進封南鄉侯。

translations.literal: At midnight the enemy indeed sent ten detachments to raid by night and burn [the camp]; Chong ambushed and crushed them and was advanced to marquis of Nanxiang.
translations.idiomatic: At midnight they sent ten companies to sneak in and torch the lines; Chong ambushed and shattered them and was enfeoffed marquis of Nanxiang.

sentences.zh: 黃初三年，假寵節鉞。

translations.literal: In the third year of Huangchu he was granted the imperial insignia and battle-axe.
translations.idiomatic: Huangchu 3 brought him the credentials of office—staff and axe.

sentences.zh: 五年，拜前將軍。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he was appointed general of the van.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he took rank as general of the van.

sentences.zh: 青龍元年，寵上疏曰：「合肥城南臨江湖，北遠壽春，賊攻圍之，得據水爲勢；

translations.literal: In the first year of Qinglong, Chong submitted a memorial saying, 'Hefei's south face adjoins the rivers and lakes, while to the north it is far from Shou-chun; when bandits attack and besiege it, they can seize the advantage of the water;
translations.idiomatic: Qinglong 1: Chong memorialized that south Hefei fronts the waterways while north lies far from Shouchun; besiegers could use the rivers;

sentences.zh: 官兵救之，當先破賊大輩，然後圍乃得解。

translations.literal: when government troops come to rescue it, they must first smash the enemy's main host, and only then can the siege be lifted.
translations.idiomatic: relief must first break the main enemy force before the siege ends.

sentences.zh: 賊往甚易，而兵往救之甚難，宜移城內之兵，其西三十里，有奇險可依，更立城以固守，此爲引賊平地而掎其歸路，於計爲便。

translations.literal: The bandits go there very easily, yet troops who go to rescue have great difficulty; it is fitting to shift the soldiers inside the city—thirty li to the west there is extraordinary terrain to rely on—and establish a new city to hold fast; this draws the bandits onto level ground and pins their line of retreat; for planning it is expedient.
translations.idiomatic: Raiders move easily; rescuers do not—so shift the garrison thirty li west to rugged ground, build a new fortress, bait the enemy onto dry land, and cut their retreat.

sentences.zh: 」護軍將軍蔣濟議，以爲：「旣示天下以弱，且望賊煙火而壞城，此爲未攻而自拔。

translations.literal: ' The protector general Jiang Ji debated, considering that 'To show the realm weakness in this way, and moreover to destroy the city at sight of the enemy's signal fires—this is to withdraw without being attacked.
translations.idiomatic: Protector general Jiang Ji objected that abandoning the old walls advertised weakness and smashing the town at the sight of enemy fires meant retreating untouched.

sentences.zh: 一至於此，劫略無限，必以淮北爲守。

translations.literal: Once it comes to this, raiding and plundering will know no limit; one will certainly have to defend along the Huai north.
translations.idiomatic: That invites limitless pillage and commits you to a Huai-north defense line.

sentences.zh: 」帝未許。

translations.literal: ' The emperor did not grant permission.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor withheld approval.

sentences.zh: 寵重表曰：「孫子言，兵者，詭道也。

translations.literal: Chong again memorialized, saying, 'Sunzi says warfare is the way of deception.
translations.idiomatic: Chong pressed again: Sunzi teaches that war is deception.

sentences.zh: 故能而示之以弱不能，驕之以利，示之以懾。

translations.literal: Therefore though able, show inability to the enemy; though unable, show ability; entice them with gain; cow them with dread.
translations.idiomatic: Feign weakness when strong and strength when weak; lure with profit and overawe with fear.

sentences.zh: 此爲形實不必相應也。

translations.literal: Thus outward form and inner reality need not correspond.
translations.idiomatic: Appearance and reality need not match.

sentences.zh: 又曰『善動敵者形之』。

translations.literal: He also says, "Those skilled at moving the enemy shape conditions for them."'
translations.idiomatic: He also wrote, "Master opponents by shaping what they see."'

sentences.zh: 今賊未至而移城却內，此所謂形而誘之也。

translations.literal: Now the bandits have not yet arrived yet we shift the city inward—this is what is called shaping conditions to lure them.
translations.idiomatic: Moving inland before they strike is shaping the battlefield to bait them.

sentences.zh: 引賊遠水，擇利而動，舉得於外，則福生於內矣。

translations.literal: Draw the bandits away from the water, strike where advantage lies—gain outside brings fortune within.
translations.idiomatic: Pull them off the rivers, strike at the advantage, and internal security follows external success.

sentences.zh: 」尚書趙咨以寵策爲長，詔遂報聽。

translations.literal: ' Minister Zhao Zi regarded Chong's plan as superior; an edict approved it.
translations.idiomatic: Minister Zhao Zi favored Chong's scheme; an edict granted consent.

sentences.zh: 其年，權自出，欲圍新城，以其遠水，積二十日不敢下舡。

translations.literal: That year Quan himself came out intending to besiege the new city; because it lay far from the water, he piled up twenty days yet dared not disembark from his boats.
translations.idiomatic: That year Sun Quan marched in person on the new fortress; it sat back from the river, so he hovered offshore twenty days without landing.

sentences.zh: 寵謂諸將曰：「權得吾移城，必於其衆中有自大之言，今大舉來欲要一切之功，雖不敢至，必當上岸耀兵以示有餘。

translations.literal: Chong said to the generals, 'When Quan learned we moved the city he must have crowed to his men; now he marches in force wanting a wholesale triumph—though he may not dare come all the way, he will surely land troops to display strength as if he had surplus power.
translations.idiomatic: Chong told his officers, 'Sun Quan boasts because we relocated; he brings a huge host for a knockout blow—he may stop short but will land soldiers to parade superiority.

sentences.zh: 」乃潛遣步騎六千，伏肥城隱處以待之。

translations.literal: ' He secretly dispatched six thousand infantry and cavalry to lie concealed near Feicheng and await them.
translations.idiomatic: He hid six thousand foot and horse near Feicheng to spring the trap.

sentences.zh: 權果上岸耀兵，寵伏軍卒起擊之，斬首數百，或有赴水死者。

translations.literal: Quan indeed landed troops to display strength; Chong's ambush suddenly rose and struck them, beheading several hundred, some drowning in the water.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan did land to show force; Chong's ambush leaped up, slew hundreds, and drove others into the drink.

sentences.zh: 明年，權自將號十萬，至合肥新城。

translations.literal: The next year Quan himself led what was proclaimed as one hundred thousand men to the new city of Hefei.
translations.idiomatic: Next year Sun Quan led an army billed at one hundred thousand against new Hefei.

sentences.zh: 寵馳往赴，募壯士數十人，折松爲炬，灌以麻油，從上風放火，燒賊攻具，射殺權弟子孫泰。

translations.literal: Chong rode swiftly to the rescue, recruited several dozen stalwarts, broke pine torches, soaked them in sesame oil, upwind set fire from above and burned the enemy siege equipment, and shot dead Quan's nephew Sun Tai.
translations.idiomatic: Chong raced thither, enlisted dozens of daredevils, fashioned pine torches soaked in oil, burned the siege gear upwind, and killed Sun Quan's nephew Sun Tai with an arrow.

sentences.zh: 賊於是引退。

translations.literal: Thereupon the bandits withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy then retired.

sentences.zh: 三年春，權遣兵數千家佃於江北。

translations.literal: In the spring of the third year Quan dispatched several thousand households to farm north of the Yangzi.
translations.idiomatic: Spring of year three he sent thousands of households to till north of the river.

sentences.zh: 至八月，寵以爲田向收孰，男女布野，其屯衞兵去城遠者數百里，可掩擊也。

translations.literal: By the eighth month Chong judged that the crops faced harvest; men and women filled the fields; garrison troops guarding the colonies farthest from the city stood several hundred li away—these could be surprised.
translations.idiomatic: By August the grain ripened and peasants thronged the fields; distant pickets lay hundreds of li out—ripe for a raid.

sentences.zh: 遣長史督三軍循江東下，摧破諸屯，焚燒穀物而還。

translations.literal: He sent the chief clerk to lead three armies down the east bank of the Yangzi, smash the colonies, burn the grain, and return.
translations.idiomatic: He sent his chief clerk with three corps downstream along the Jiang to wreck the settlements, torch the grain, and withdraw.

sentences.zh: 詔羙之，因以所獲盡爲將士賞。

translations.literal: An edict praised him and therefore devoted all the booty to rewarding officers and soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial praise followed, and every captured prize went to the troops as bounty.

sentences.zh: 田豫字國讓，漁陽雍奴人也。

translations.literal: Tian Yu's courtesy name was Guorang; he was a man of Yongnu in Yuyang.
translations.idiomatic: Tian Yu, courtesy name Guorang, hailed from Yongnu in Yuyang.

sentences.zh: 劉備之奔公孫瓚也，豫時年少，自託於備，備甚奇之。

translations.literal: When Liu Bei fled to Gongsun Zan, Yu was still young and entrusted himself to Bei; Bei greatly esteemed him.
translations.idiomatic: While Liu Bei sheltered with Gongsun Zan, the youthful Tian Yu attached himself to Bei, who thought him extraordinary.

sentences.zh: 備爲豫州刺史，豫以母老求歸，備涕泣與別，曰：「恨不與君共成大事也。」

translations.literal: When Bei became inspector of Yu Province, Yu sought to return home because his mother was aged; Bei wept as they parted, saying, 'I regret that I cannot with you accomplish the great enterprise.'
translations.idiomatic: After Bei became inspector of Yu Province, Tian Yu asked leave—his mother was old. They parted in tears as Bei said, 'How I wish we could finish the great work together.'

sentences.zh: 公孫瓚使豫守東州令，瓚將王門叛瓚，爲袁紹將萬餘人來攻。

translations.literal: Gongsun Zan ordered Yu to defend district magistrate of Dongzhou; Zan's general Wang Men rebelled against Zan and, as Yuan Shao's officer, brought more than ten thousand men to attack.
translations.idiomatic: Gongsun Zan assigned Tian Yu magistrate of Dongzhou; Wang Men rebelled, joined Yuan Shao, and marched over ten thousand men against the town.

sentences.zh: 衆懼欲降。

translations.literal: The multitude feared and wished to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: The defenders panicked and wanted to yield.

sentences.zh: 豫登城謂門曰：「卿爲公孫所厚而去，意有所不得已也；

translations.literal: Yu ascended the wall and said to Men, 'You were generously treated by Gongsun yet departed—in your mind there was something you could not help;
translations.idiomatic: Tian Yu mounted the wall and shouted to Wang Men, 'Gongsun Zan favored you; you left because you were desperate;

sentences.zh: 今還作賊，乃知卿亂人耳。

translations.literal: now having returned to act the bandit, I now know you are a man who throws the realm into disorder.
translations.idiomatic: now you turn bandit—plainly you are a wrecker of order.

sentences.zh: 夫挈瓶之智，守不假器，吾旣受之矣；

translations.literal: The wisdom that fills a pitcher—holding a post borrows no other's vessel—I have already accepted [this duty];
translations.idiomatic: A petty wit may guard a well—you received this office; I hold it now;

sentences.zh: 何不急攻乎？

translations.literal: why do you not press the assault vigorously?'
translations.idiomatic: why not storm it while you can?'

sentences.zh: 」門慙而退。

translations.literal: ' Men was ashamed and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Shamed, Wang Men broke off the attack.

sentences.zh: 瓚雖知豫有權謀而不能任也。

translations.literal: Though Zan knew Yu had stratagems he could not employ him.
translations.idiomatic: Zan knew Tian Yu was shrewd yet never gave him real responsibility.

sentences.zh: 瓚敗而鮮于輔爲國人所推，行太守事，素善豫，以爲長史。

translations.literal: When Zan was defeated Xianyu Fu was pushed forward by the people of the state to conduct grand administrator affairs; being long friendly with Yu, he appointed him chief clerk.
translations.idiomatic: After Zan's fall Xianyu Fu ran the commandery at popular insistence; fond of Tian Yu, he made him chief clerk.

sentences.zh: 時雄傑並起，輔莫知所從。

translations.literal: At that time heroes rose together and Fu did not know whom to follow.
translations.idiomatic: Heroes rose on every side and Fu wavered between them.

sentences.zh: 豫謂輔曰：「終能定天下者，必曹氏也。

translations.literal: Yu said to Fu, 'The one who in the end will settle the realm must be the house of Cao.
translations.idiomatic: Tian Yu told him, 'The house that will reunify the realm will be Cao Cao's.

sentences.zh: 宜速歸命，無後禍期。

translations.literal: You ought swiftly to submit—do not await later disaster.'
translations.idiomatic: Submit soon—do not invite later ruin.'

sentences.zh: 」輔從其計，用受封寵。

translations.literal: ' Fu followed his plan and thereby received enfeoffment and favor.
translations.idiomatic: Fu took the advice and earned title and favor.

sentences.zh: 太祖召豫爲丞相軍謀掾，除頴陰、朗陵令，遷弋陽太守，所在有治。

translations.literal: The Founding Emperor summoned Yu as strategic adviser to the chancellor's army, appointed him magistrate of Yingyin and Langling, promoted him grand administrator of Yiyang, and wherever he went his governance was effective.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao enlisted him as army strategist, named him magistrate of Yingyin and Langling, raised him to administrator of Yiyang, and his administration prospered everywhere.

sentences.zh: 鄢陵侯彰征代郡，以豫爲相。

translations.literal: Marquis Yanling Zhang campaigned against Dai commandery and appointed Yu chief of staff.
translations.idiomatic: When Marquis of Yanling Cao Zhang attacked Dai commandery, Tian Yu served as chief of staff.

sentences.zh: 軍次易北，虜伏騎擊之，軍人擾亂，莫知所爲。

translations.literal: The army halted north of Yi; barbarians ambushed with cavalry and struck them; the soldiers fell into confusion and knew not what to do.
translations.idiomatic: North of Yi barbarian horse archers ambushed the column; the ranks dissolved in panic.

sentences.zh: 豫因地形，回車結圜陣，弓弩持滿於內，疑兵塞其隙。

translations.literal: Yu exploited the terrain, turned the wagons and formed a circular formation, filled the interior with crossbows at full draw, and blocked the gaps with decoy troops.
translations.idiomatic: Tian Yu used the ground to wheel wagons into a ring, packed crossbowmen inside, and plugged gaps with feints.

sentences.zh: 胡不能進，散去。

translations.literal: The Hu could not advance and dispersed.
translations.idiomatic: The tribesmen stalled and scattered.

sentences.zh: 追擊，大破之，遂前平代，皆豫策也。

translations.literal: They pursued and smashed them, then advanced to pacify Dai—all Yu's strategy.
translations.idiomatic: A pursuit routed them; the Dai campaign succeeded—credit belonged to Tian Yu.

sentences.zh: 遷南陽太守。

translations.literal: He was promoted to grand administrator of Nanyang.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to grand administrator of Nanyang.

sentences.zh: 先時，郡人侯音反，衆數千人在山中爲群盜，大爲郡患。

translations.literal: Previously a man of the commandery, Hou Yin, rebelled; several thousand men in the mountains formed bandit gangs and greatly plagued the commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Hou Yin of the commandery had risen in revolt; thousands of men took to the hills as bandits and terrorized the district.

sentences.zh: 前太守收其黨與五百餘人，表奏皆當死。

translations.literal: The former grand administrator seized more than five hundred of his accomplices and memorialized that all deserved death.
translations.idiomatic: His predecessor had arrested over five hundred accomplices and petitioned for the execution of every one.

sentences.zh: 豫悉見諸繫囚，慰喻，開其自新之路，一時破械遣之。

translations.literal: Yu interviewed all the prisoners in fetters, comforted and instructed them, opened a path by which they might reform, at once broke their shackles, and sent them away.
translations.idiomatic: Tian Yu visited every chained captive, spoke reassurance, offered them a fresh start, struck off their bonds, and released them.

sentences.zh: 諸囚皆叩頭，願自效，即相告語，群賊一朝解散，郡內清靜。

translations.literal: The prisoners all kowtowed, wished to prove their loyalty, informed one another, and the bandit gangs dissolved in one morning; within the commandery there was quiet.
translations.idiomatic: They kowtowed, pledged service, spread the word among themselves, and the outlaw bands melted away overnight; peace returned to the commandery.

sentences.zh: 具以狀上，太祖善之。

translations.literal: He reported the full circumstances upward; the Founding Emperor approved.
translations.idiomatic: He forwarded a full report; Cao Cao approved.

sentences.zh: 文帝初，北狄彊盛，侵擾邊塞，乃使豫持節護烏丸校尉，牽招、解儁并護鮮卑。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Wen's reign the northern Di were strong and harassed the frontier passes; therefore Yu was sent bearing credentials as protector colonel of the Wuhuan, while Qian Zhao and Xie Jun jointly supervised the Xianbei.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Cao Pi's reign the northern tribes pressed the frontier, so Tian Yu took the staff as Wuhuan colonel while Qian Zhao and Xie Jun oversaw the Xianbei.

sentences.zh: 自高柳以東，濊貊以西，鮮卑數十部，比能、彌加、素利割地統御，各有分界；

translations.literal: From Gaoliu eastward and Huimo westward were several tens of Xianbei divisions—Bineng, Mijia, and Suli—who partitioned territory and ruled, each with its boundaries;
translations.idiomatic: East of Gaoliu and west of the Huimo tribes stretched dozens of Xianbei bands—Bineng, Mijia, Suli—each ruling a slice of ground with fixed borders;

sentences.zh: 乃共誓要，皆不得以馬與中國市。

translations.literal: they jointly swore an oath that none might trade horses with the Central States.
translations.idiomatic: they swore jointly not to sell horses into China.

sentences.zh: 豫以戎狄爲一，非中國之利，乃先搆離之，使自爲讎敵，互相攻伐。

translations.literal: Yu considered the Rong and Di united as one thing disadvantageous to the Central States; therefore he first sowed discord among them, causing them to become mutual foes and attack one another.
translations.idiomatic: Tian Yu judged a unified frontier bad for the realm and set the tribes at each other's throats before they could unite.

sentences.zh: 素利違盟，出馬千匹與官，爲比能所攻，求救於豫。

translations.literal: Suli violated the covenant and sent out one thousand horses to the authorities; attacked by Bineng, he begged Yu for rescue.
translations.idiomatic: Suli broke the pact by selling a thousand mounts to the court; Bineng attacked him, and he pleaded with Tian Yu for aid.

sentences.zh: 豫恐遂相兼并，爲害滋深，宜救善討惡，示信衆狄。

translations.literal: Yu feared they would then annex one another and harm would grow deeper—it was fitting to rescue the good and punish the wicked, displaying good faith to the many Di.
translations.idiomatic: He feared unchecked annexation and worse raids—better to aid the righteous, punish the vicious, and signal honesty to every tribe.

sentences.zh: 單將銳卒，深入虜庭，胡人衆多，鈔軍前後，斷截歸路。

translations.literal: Leading picked troops alone he penetrated deep into barbarian territory; the Hu were numerous, raiding his army front and rear and cutting off his line of retreat.
translations.idiomatic: With only elite soldiers he drove deep into tribal lands; nomads swarmed fore and aft and severed his retreat.

sentences.zh: 豫乃進軍，去虜十餘里結屯營，多聚牛馬糞然之，從他道引去。

translations.literal: Yu therefore advanced, halted ten-odd li from the barbarians and formed an encampment, piled much cattle and horse dung and set it burning, then withdrew by another route.
translations.idiomatic: He camped a dozen li from the enemy, heaped dung alight as a blind, and slipped away along another track.

sentences.zh: 胡見煙火不絕，以爲尚在，去，行數十里乃知之。

translations.literal: The Hu saw smoke and fire unceasing and thought Yu was still there; after they left and marched several tens of li they realized.
translations.idiomatic: The tribesmen saw endless smoke and assumed he remained; only after marching many li did they discover the ruse.

sentences.zh: 追豫到馬城，圍之十重，豫密嚴，使司馬建旌旗，鳴鼓吹，將步騎從南門出，胡人皆屬目往赴之。

translations.literal: Pursuing Yu to Ma city they surrounded him tenfold; Yu maintained strict secrecy, ordered a major to raise banners and beat drums and blow horns, and led infantry and cavalry out the south gate—all the Hu fixed their eyes and rushed thither.
translations.idiomatic: They chased him to Ma city and ringed him ten deep; he hid his plan, had a major parade colors and music out the south gate, and every tribesman rushed that way.

sentences.zh: 豫將精銳自北門出，鼓譟而起，兩頭俱發，出虜不意，虜衆散亂，皆棄弓馬步走，追討二十餘里，僵尸蔽地。

translations.literal: Yu led crack troops out the north gate, rose with shouting battle cries, struck from both ends—the barbarians did not expect it; the barbarian host scattered in confusion, all abandoning bows and horses and fleeing on foot; pursuit continued twenty-odd li and corpses covered the ground.
translations.idiomatic: He struck from the north with picked men and a sudden battle cry; caught between two fires the nomads broke, dropped weapons and mounts, and fled on foot; the chase ran twenty li and left the plain strewn with dead.

sentences.zh: 又烏丸王骨進桀黠不恭，豫因出塞案行，單將麾下百餘騎入進部。

translations.literal: Moreover the Wuhuan king Gu Jin was fierce and disrespectful; Yu therefore went beyond the frontier on inspection, leading only a bit over one hundred horsemen of his command into Jin's camp.
translations.idiomatic: The Wuhuan chief Gu Jin was arrogant and rude; Tian Yu rode beyond the pass on patrol with barely a hundred horse and walked into Jin's camp.

sentences.zh: 進逆拜，遂使左右斬進，顯其罪惡以令衆。

translations.literal: Jin came forward to pay homage; Yu then ordered his attendants to execute Jin, displaying his crimes and wickedness to command the multitude.
translations.idiomatic: When Jin stepped up to bow, Tian Yu had guards cut him down and parade his crimes before the assembly.

sentences.zh: 衆皆怖慴不敢動，便以進弟代進。

translations.literal: The multitude were all frightened and dared not move; thereupon he installed Jin's younger brother in Jin's place.
translations.idiomatic: The horde froze in terror; he installed Jin's younger brother as chief.

sentences.zh: 自是胡人破膽，威震沙漠。

translations.literal: From this the Hu lost courage and his might shook the desert.
translations.idiomatic: After that the tribes lost heart and his name shook the desert.

sentences.zh: 山賊高艾，衆數千人，寇鈔，爲幽、冀害，豫誘使鮮卑素利部斬艾，傳首京都。

translations.literal: The mountain bandit Gao Ai had several thousand followers who raided and plundered, harming You and Ji; Yu induced Suli's Xianbei band to behead Ai and sent the head to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: The brigand Gao Ai led thousands in raids across You and Ji; Tian Yu persuaded Suli's Xianbei to execute him and shipped the head to Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 封豫長樂亭侯。

translations.literal: Yu was enfeoffed village marquis of Changle.
translations.idiomatic: He received the village marquisate of Changle.

sentences.zh: 爲校尉九年，其御夷狄，恒摧抑兼并，乖散彊猾。

translations.literal: Serving nine years as colonel, in controlling the Yi and Di he constantly crushed annexation and scattered the strong and cunning.
translations.idiomatic: Nine years as colonel he broke up mergers among tribes and scattered the strongest intriguers.

sentences.zh: 凡逋亡姦宄，爲胡作計不利官者，豫皆構刺攪離，使凶邪之謀不遂，聚居之類不安。

translations.literal: All fugitives and villains who plotted with the Hu against the official interest—Yu all sowed discord and drove apart so that evil schemes failed and settled communities could not rest secure.
translations.idiomatic: Fugitives who connived with nomads against the court—he set them at odds until plots collapsed and hostile camps could not endure.

sentences.zh: 事業未究，而幽州刺史王雄支黨欲令雄領烏丸校尉，毀豫亂邊，爲國生事。

translations.literal: Before his task was finished the You provincial governor Wang Xiong's faction wished to make Xiong hold the Wuhuan colonelcy; they slandered Yu as disturbing the frontier and creating trouble for the state.
translations.idiomatic: Before he finished, Governor Wang Xiong's clique wanted Xiong named Wuhuan colonel and smeared Tian Yu as a troublemaker on the border.

sentences.zh: 遂轉豫爲汝南太守，加殄夷將軍。

translations.literal: Thereupon Yu was transferred to grand administrator of Runan with the additional title general who Exterminates the Yi.
translations.idiomatic: He was shifted to Runan with the brevet rank of general who Exterminates the Yi.

sentences.zh: 太和末，公孫淵以遼東叛，帝欲征之而難其人，中領軍楊曁舉豫應選。

translations.literal: At the end of the Taihe reign Gongsun Yuan rebelled in Liaodong; the emperor wished to campaign against him but found no man for it; central commander Yang Ji nominated Yu for selection.
translations.idiomatic: Late in Taihe Gongsun Yuan rebelled in Liaodong; the emperor wanted a commander and Yang Ji recommended Tian Yu.

sentences.zh: 〈臣松之案：曁字休先，熒陽人，事見

translations.literal: 〈Your servant Songzhi investigates: Ji's courtesy name was Xiuxian, a man of Yingyang; his affairs are seen in
translations.idiomatic: 〈Pei Songzhi notes: Yang Ji, courtesy Xiuxian, from Yingyang—his career appears in

sentences.zh: 〈劉曄傳〉

translations.literal: 〈Biography of Liu Ye〉
translations.idiomatic: the biography of Liu Ye.〉

translations.literal: Period mark ending the citation sentence.
translations.idiomatic: This closes Pei Songzhi's gloss.

sentences.zh: 曁子肇，晉荊州刺史。

translations.literal: Ji's son Zhao became inspector of Jing Province under Jin.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yang Zhao served as inspector of Jing Province under the Jin.

sentences.zh: 山濤啟事稱肇有才能。

translations.literal: Shan Tao's memorial praised Zhao's talent.
translations.idiomatic: Shan Tao's memorial praised Yang Zhao's abilities.

sentences.zh: 肇子潭字道元，次歆字公嗣，潭子彧字長文，次經字仲武，皆見《潘岳集》。〉

translations.literal: Zhao's son Tan, courtesy name Daoyuan; next Xin, courtesy name Gongsi; Tan's son Yu, courtesy name Changwen; next Jing, courtesy name Zhongwu—all appear in Pan Yue's collected works.〉
translations.idiomatic: Zhao's son Tan (Daoyuan), Xin (Gongsi); Tan's son Yu (Changwen) and Jing (Zhongwu)—all mentioned in Pan Yue's writings.〉

sentences.zh: 乃使豫以本官督青州諸軍，假節，往討之。

translations.literal: Thereupon Yu was ordered in his existing office to supervise Qingzhou forces, granted credentials, and sent to attack.
translations.idiomatic: The court kept him in grade, gave him Qingzhou command, the staff of authority, and orders to strike.

sentences.zh: 會吳賊遣使與淵相結，帝以賊衆多，又以渡海，詔豫使罷軍。

translations.literal: When Wu bandits sent envoys to ally with Yuan, the emperor thought the bandits numerous and crossing the sea difficult; he ordered Yu to disband the army.
translations.idiomatic: When Wu allied with Yuan, the emperor feared both enemy numbers and the sea crossing and told Tian Yu to stand down.

sentences.zh: 豫度賊船垂還，歲晚風急，必畏漂浪，東隨無岸，當赴成山。

translations.literal: Yu calculated that the enemy ships were about to return; at year's end the wind would be fierce—they must fear drifting waves; eastward along the coast there was no shore—they would head for Cheng Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: Tian Yu reckoned the fleet would turn homeward in late year's bitter gales; with no lee east along the coast they would run for Cheng Mountain.

sentences.zh: 成山無藏船之處，輙便循海，案行地形，及諸山島，徼截險要，列兵屯守。

translations.literal: Cheng Mountain had nowhere to hide ships; he simply followed the coast, surveying terrain and the various mountain islands, intercepting at narrows and posting troops to hold them.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng Mountain offered no anchorage, so he shadowed the shore, mapped headlands and islets, and sealed the choke points with troops.

sentences.zh: 自入成山，登漢武之觀。

translations.literal: Entering Cheng Mountain he ascended Emperor Wu of Han's lookout.
translations.idiomatic: He entered Cheng Mountain and climbed the lookout Han Wudi had used.

sentences.zh: 賊還，果遇惡風，船皆觸山沈沒，波蕩著岸，無所蒙竄，盡虜其衆。

translations.literal: When the bandits returned they indeed met foul winds; ships all struck mountains and sank or were dashed ashore with nowhere to flee—all their forces were captured.
translations.idiomatic: The fleet met the feared storm; hulls smashed on cliffs or surf; crews could not escape and were taken wholesale.

sentences.zh: 初，諸將皆笑於空地待賊，及賊破，競欲與謀，求入海鉤取浪舡。

translations.literal: At first the generals had laughed at waiting for bandits on empty ground; when the bandits were broken they all wished to join the planning and requested to go to sea to hook up sunken boats.
translations.idiomatic: Generals had mocked his empty-ground trap; after the victory they clamored to ride salvagers out and snag wrecks.

sentences.zh: 豫懼窮虜死戰，皆不聽。

translations.literal: Yu feared desperate barbarians fighting to the death and permitted none of it.
translations.idiomatic: He refused—cornered foes would fight to the death.

sentences.zh: 初，豫以太守督青州，青州刺史程喜內懷不服，軍事之際，多相違錯。

translations.literal: Earlier Yu as grand administrator supervised Qingzhou; provincial governor Cheng Xi inwardly refused submission—during military affairs they often contradicted each other.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, as administrator overseeing Qingzhou, he crossed Cheng Xi the provincial governor, who quietly resisted and second-guessed every operation.

sentences.zh: 喜知帝寶愛明珠，乃密上：「豫雖有戰功而禁令寬弛，所得器仗珠金甚多，放散皆不納官。

translations.literal: Xi knew the emperor treasured bright pearls and secretly memorialized: Though Yu has battle merit his prohibitions are lax; weapons and pearl gold obtained are very many yet he releases them all without turning them over to the treasury.
translations.idiomatic: Xi knew the sovereign loved pearls and impeached Tian Yu: victories aside, discipline was slack—loot in arms and pearls never reached the treasury.

sentences.zh: 」由是功不見列。

translations.literal: Therefore his merit was not listed.
translations.idiomatic: His exploits went uncredited.

sentences.zh: 後孫權號十萬衆攻新城，征東將軍滿寵欲率諸軍救之。

translations.literal: Later Sun Quan with what was proclaimed as one hundred thousand attacked the new city; east-conquering general Man Chong wished to lead the various armies to rescue it.
translations.idiomatic: Later Sun Quan marched on the new fortress with an army billed at one hundred thousand; Man Chong wanted to march every corps to relieve it.

sentences.zh: 豫曰：「賊悉衆大舉，非徒投射小利，欲質新城以致大軍耳。

translations.literal: Yu said: The bandits have raised their whole host in a great thrust—they do not merely shoot for petty gain; they wish to pin down the new city to draw the great army.
translations.idiomatic: Tian Yu argued: Quan commits his whole strength—not for a skirmish but to nail our fortress and lure the main host.

sentences.zh: 宜聽使攻城，挫其銳氣，不當與爭鋒也。

translations.literal: It is fitting to let them assault the city and blunt their keen edge—one ought not contend sharpness with them.
translations.idiomatic: Let them grind against the walls and dull their edge; do not trade blows on their terms.

sentences.zh: 城不可拔，衆必罷怠；

translations.literal: If the city cannot be taken the masses must weary;
translations.idiomatic: Fail to storm it and their troops tire;

sentences.zh: 罷怠然後擊之，可大克也。

translations.literal: when they weary then strike them—you can achieve a great victory.
translations.idiomatic: strike when exhaustion sets in and you win big.

sentences.zh: 若賊見計，必不攻城，勢將自走。

translations.literal: If the bandits see through the plan they will surely not attack the city—the momentum will make them withdraw of themselves.
translations.idiomatic: If they see through it they may not invest the fortress at all and will slip away on their own.

sentences.zh: 若便進兵，適入其計。

translations.literal: If one rashly advances troops one falls straight into their plan.
translations.idiomatic: Send relief now and you step into their trap.

sentences.zh: 又大軍相向，當使難知，不當使自畫也。

translations.literal: Moreover when great armies face each other one ought to make planning difficult for them—not let them map their own course.
translations.idiomatic: When hosts collide you should cloud their counsel, not hand them a script.

sentences.zh: 」豫輙上狀，天子從之。

translations.literal: Yu promptly submitted the situation; the Son of Heaven followed him.
translations.idiomatic: He rushed the analysis to court; the emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 會賊遁走。

translations.literal: When it happened the bandits fled.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy withdrew as predicted.

sentences.zh: 後吳復來寇，豫往拒之，賊即退。

translations.literal: Later Wu came again to raid; Yu went to resist them and the bandits at once withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Wu raided again; Tian Yu met them and they retreated at once.

sentences.zh: 諸軍夜驚，云：「賊復來！

translations.literal: The various armies panicked at night, crying The bandits have come again!
translations.idiomatic: That night the camps cried panic: 'They are back!'

sentences.zh: 」豫卧不起，令衆「敢動者斬」。

translations.literal: Yu lay down and would not rise, ordering the troops Whoever moves shall be executed.
translations.idiomatic: Tian Yu stayed abed and ordered: 'The next man who stirs dies.'

sentences.zh: 有頃，竟無賊。

translations.literal: After a while there proved to be no bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Soon it was clear no foe had come.

sentences.zh: 景初末，增邑三百，并前五百戶。

translations.literal: At the end of Jingchu his fief was increased by three hundred households, together with the previous five hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: Late in Jingchu his estate gained three hundred households atop the existing five hundred.

sentences.zh: 正始初，遷使持節護匈奴中郎將，加振威將軍，領并州刺史。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhengshi he was promoted to bearer of credentials as protector colonel of the Xiongnu and general who Inspires Might, concurrently inspector of Bing Province.
translations.idiomatic: Early Zhengshi brought the staff as Xiongnu colonel, rank as Inspires Might general, and the Bingzhou inspectorship.

sentences.zh: 外胡聞其威名，相率來獻。

translations.literal: Foreign Hu hearing his awesome reputation came in succession to present tribute.
translations.idiomatic: Frontier tribes heard his name and queued up with tribute.

sentences.zh: 州界寧肅，百姓懷之。

translations.literal: The province's borders were tranquil and the hundred surnames cherished him.
translations.idiomatic: The province quieted and the people loved him.

sentences.zh: 徵爲衞尉。

translations.literal: He was summoned as chamberlain for the palace garrison.
translations.idiomatic: The court called him to the chamberlainship of the palace guard.

sentences.zh: 屢乞遜位，太傅司馬宣王以爲豫克壯，書喻未聽。

translations.literal: Repeatedly begging to yield office, grand tutor Sima Yi considered Yu still vigorous and wrote urging him—permission was not granted.
translations.idiomatic: He begged to retire again and again; Sima Yi called him hale and refused.

sentences.zh: 豫書荅曰：「年過七十而以居位，譬猶鍾鳴漏盡而夜行不休，是罪人也。

translations.literal: Yu wrote in reply: Past seventy yet holding office is like the bell having sounded and the clepsydra having run out yet traveling by night without cease—such a one is a criminal.
translations.idiomatic: He answered: 'After seventy to cling to office is like ringing midnight bells yet racing through the dark—that is crime.'

sentences.zh: 」遂固稱疾篤。

translations.literal: Thereupon he firmly pleaded grave illness.
translations.idiomatic: He then insisted he was mortally ill.

sentences.zh: 拜太中大夫，食卿祿。

translations.literal: He was appointed grand counselor of the palace with salary of a minister.
translations.idiomatic: They named him grand counselor with a minister's stipend.

sentences.zh: 年八十二薨。

translations.literal: At age eighty-two he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died at eighty-two.

sentences.zh: 子彭祖嗣。

translations.literal: His son Pengzu succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Tian Pengzu inherited the title.

sentences.zh: 〈《魏略》曰：豫罷官歸，居魏縣。

translations.literal: 《魏略》 says: When Yu left office and returned he dwelt in Wei county.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei lüe records: after retiring Tian Yu lived in Wei county.

sentences.zh: 會汝南遣健步詣征北，感豫宿恩，過拜之。

translations.literal: When Runan dispatched a swift courier to the north-conquering command, moved by Yu's old kindness he stopped to pay respects.
translations.idiomatic: Runan sent a runner north; remembering Tian Yu's past kindness he detoured to bow.

sentences.zh: 豫爲殺雞炊黍，送詣至陌頭，謂之曰：「罷老，苦汝來過。

translations.literal: Yu killed a chicken and cooked millet for him, escorted him to the edge of the road, saying to him: I am old and retired—it pains me that you came such a distance.
translations.idiomatic: Tian Yu killed a fowl, steamed millet, walked him to the road, and said: 'I am a useless old man—sorry you came so far.'

sentences.zh: 無能有益，若何？

translations.literal: I cannot benefit you—what is to be done?
translations.idiomatic: I have nothing to give you—what can I do?'

sentences.zh: 」健步愍其貧羸，流涕而去，還爲故吏民說之。

translations.literal: The swift courier pitied his poverty and emaciation, left weeping, and on returning told the former clerks and people.
translations.idiomatic: The runner wept at his poverty and thin frame; back home he told the old staff and townsfolk.

sentences.zh: 汝南爲具資數千匹，遣人餉豫，豫一不受。

translations.literal: Runan prepared several thousand bolts of goods for him and sent men to present them to Yu—Yu accepted none.
translations.idiomatic: Runan raised thousands in goods to send; Tian Yu refused every gift.

sentences.zh: 會病，立戒其妻子曰：「葬我必於西門豹邊。

translations.literal: When he fell ill he immediately instructed his wife and children: When you bury me it must be beside Ximen Bao.
translations.idiomatic: Falling ill, he told his family: 'Bury me beside Ximen Bao.'

sentences.zh: 」妻之難之，言：「西門豹古之神人，那可葬於其邊乎？

translations.literal: His wife found this difficult and said: Ximen Bao is an ancient divine man—how can one bury beside him?
translations.idiomatic: His wife protested: 'Ximen Bao was a godlike sage—how dare we lie beside him?'

sentences.zh: 」豫言：「豹所履行與我敵等耳，使死而有靈，必與我善。

translations.literal: Yu said: What Bao practiced stands equal to mine; if the dead have spirits he will surely treat me kindly.
translations.idiomatic: He said: 'His conduct matches mine; if spirits endure we shall be friends.'

sentences.zh: 」妻子從之。

translations.literal: Wife and children obeyed.
translations.idiomatic: They did as he asked.

sentences.zh: 汝南聞其死也，悲之，旣爲畫像，又就爲立碑銘。〉

translations.literal: Runan hearing of his death grieved; they painted his likeness and moreover erected an inscribed stele for him.〉
translations.idiomatic: Runan mourned him, commissioned his portrait, and raised an inscribed stone.〉

sentences.zh: 豫清儉約素，賞賜皆散之將士。

translations.literal: Yu was pure, frugal, and plain; rewards and gifts he distributed to officers and soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: Tian Yu lived plainly and passed every bonus to the ranks.

sentences.zh: 每胡、狄私遺，悉簿藏官，不入家；

translations.literal: Whenever Hu and Di privately presented gifts he recorded them all for storage with the authorities—nothing entered his household;
translations.idiomatic: Nomad gifts went straight onto the ledgers for the government—never his purse;

sentences.zh: 家常貧匱。

translations.literal: his household was constantly poor and wanting.
translations.idiomatic: his own house stayed threadbare.

sentences.zh: 雖殊類，咸高豫節。

translations.literal: Though of alien races they all esteemed Yu's integrity.
translations.idiomatic: Even foreigners honored his rectitude.

sentences.zh: 〈《魏略》曰：鮮卑素利等數來客見，多以牛馬遺豫；

translations.literal: 《魏略》 says: Suli and others of the Xianbei came several times as guests to visit; many times they presented cattle and horses to Yu;
translations.idiomatic: The Wei lüe adds: Suli's Xianbei visited often and loaded him with cattle and horses;

sentences.zh: 豫轉送官。

translations.literal: Yu forwarded them to the authorities.
translations.idiomatic: Tian Yu forwarded each herd to the treasury.

sentences.zh: 胡以爲前所與豫物顯露，不如持金。

translations.literal: The Hu thought what they had previously given Yu was conspicuous—better to hold gold.
translations.idiomatic: The tribes decided livestock was too obvious and switched to gold.

sentences.zh: 乃密懷金三十斤，謂豫曰：「願避左右，我欲有所道。

translations.literal: Thereupon they secretly carried thirty jin of gold and said to Yu: We wish you to dismiss attendants left and right—we have something to say.
translations.idiomatic: They hid thirty jin of gold and asked for privacy.

sentences.zh: 」豫從之，胡因跪曰：「我見公貧，故前後遺公牛馬，公輒送官，今密以此上公，可以爲家資。

translations.literal: Yu complied; the Hu therefore knelt and said: We see your lordship poor; therefore before and after we gave oxen and horses but your lordship always sent them to the authorities; now we secretly present this to your lordship—it can serve as household capital.
translations.idiomatic: Tian Yu cleared the room; they knelt and said: 'We knew you were poor—every herd went to the court; take this gold for your household.'

sentences.zh: 」豫張袖受之，荅其厚意。

translations.literal: Yu spread his sleeve and accepted it, acknowledging their generous intent.
translations.idiomatic: He opened his sleeve, took the gold, and thanked them.

sentences.zh: 胡去之後，皆悉付外，具以狀聞。

translations.literal: After the Hu departed he turned it all over outside and fully reported the circumstances.
translations.idiomatic: When they left he wired every ounce to the authorities with a full memorial.

sentences.zh: 於是詔褒之曰：「昔魏絳開懷以納戎賂，今卿舉袖以受狄金，朕甚嘉焉。

translations.literal: Thereupon an edict praised him: In antiquity Wei Jiang opened his bosom to accept Rong bribes; now you raise your sleeve to receive Di gold—we greatly approve.
translations.idiomatic: An edict praised him: 'Wei Jiang once welcomed barbarian gifts with open arms; you mirror him—we applaud this.'

sentences.zh: 」乃即賜絹五百匹。

translations.literal: Thereupon he was gifted five hundred bolts of silk.
translations.idiomatic: The throne sent five hundred bolts of silk.

sentences.zh: 豫得賜，分以其半藏小府，後胡復來，以半與之。〉

translations.literal: Yu receiving the gift divided half to store in the lesser treasury; later when the Hu came again he gave them half.〉
translations.idiomatic: He banked half in the lesser treasury and returned half on their next visit.〉

sentences.zh: 嘉平六年，下詔襃揚，賜其家錢糓。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Jiaping an edict praised him and gifted his household cash and grain.
translations.idiomatic: Jiaping 6 brought another imperial commendation and grants of coin and grain to his family.

sentences.zh: 語在

translations.literal: The wording is in
translations.idiomatic: The passage continues in

sentences.zh: 〈徐邈傳〉

translations.literal: 〈Biography of Xu Miao〉
translations.idiomatic: the biography of Xu Miao.

translations.literal: Period mark ending the cross-reference.
translations.idiomatic: This ends the citation pointer.

sentences.zh: 牽招字子經，安平觀津人也。

translations.literal: Qian Zhao's courtesy name was Zijing; he was a man of Guanjin in Anping.
translations.idiomatic: Qian Zhao, courtesy Zijing, came from Guanjin in Anping.

sentences.zh: 年十餘歲，詣同縣樂隱受學。

translations.literal: At age ten-odd sui he went to the same county's Le Yin to receive schooling.
translations.idiomatic: In his teens he studied under Le Yin of the same county.

sentences.zh: 後隱爲車騎將軍何苗長史，招隨卒業。

translations.literal: Later Yin became chief clerk to general of chariots and cavalry He Miao, and Zhao followed him to complete his studies.
translations.idiomatic: Le Yin later served He Miao as chief clerk; Qian Zhao stayed on to finish his schooling.

sentences.zh: 值京都亂，苗、隱見害，招俱與隱門生史路等觸蹈鋒刃，共殯斂隱屍，送喪還歸。

translations.literal: When the capital fell into turmoil Miao and Yin were killed; Zhao together with Yin's disciple Shi Lu and others braved blades, jointly laid Yin out for burial, and escorted the funeral home.
translations.idiomatic: Amid the capital's chaos both He Miao and Le Yin died; Qian Zhao joined Le Yin's pupil Shi Lu in dodging steel to prepare the corpse and bear the bier home.

sentences.zh: 道遇寇鈔，路等皆悉散走。

translations.literal: On the road they encountered bandits raiding; Lu and the others all fled in scatter.
translations.idiomatic: Bandits waylaid them on the road and Shi Lu's party scattered in flight.

sentences.zh: 賊欲斫棺取釘，招垂淚請赦。

translations.literal: The bandits wished to chop the coffin to take the nails; Zhao wept and begged forgiveness.
translations.idiomatic: The robbers meant to splinter the coffin for the nails; Qian Zhao wept and pleaded for mercy.

sentences.zh: 賊義之，乃釋而去。

translations.literal: The bandits deemed him righteous and therefore released him and departed.
translations.idiomatic: They respected his valor and let him pass.

sentences.zh: 由此顯名。

translations.literal: From this his name became renowned.
translations.idiomatic: His reputation dates from that ordeal.

sentences.zh: 冀州牧袁紹辟爲督軍從事，兼領烏丸突騎。

translations.literal: Governor of Ji Province Yuan Shao summoned him as aide for supervising the army and concurrently commanded Wuhuan shock cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Shao of Ji Province employed him as army-staff supervisor and put him over Wuhuan mounted raiders.

sentences.zh: 紹舍人犯令，招先斬乃白，紹奇其意而不見罪也。

translations.literal: A steward of Shao violated regulations; Zhao first executed him then reported—Shao marveled at his intent and did not punish him.
translations.idiomatic: When one of Yuan Shao's household broke the law Qian Zhao executed him first and reported afterward; Shao admired the nerve and held him blameless.

sentences.zh: 紹卒，又事紹子尚。

translations.literal: When Shao died he again served Shao's son Shang.
translations.idiomatic: After Yuan Shao died he served Yuan Shang.

sentences.zh: 建安九年，太祖圍鄴。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Jian'an the Founding Emperor besieged Ye.
translations.idiomatic: Jian'an 9: Cao Cao invested Ye.

sentences.zh: 尚遣招至上黨，督致軍糧。

translations.literal: Shang dispatched Zhao to Shangdang to supervise delivery of army grain.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Shang sent him to Shangdang to rush grain to the army.

sentences.zh: 未還，尚破走，到中山。

translations.literal: Before Zhao returned Shang was defeated and fled to Zhongshan.
translations.idiomatic: Before he could return Yuan Shang had been routed and fled to Zhongshan.

sentences.zh: 時尚外兄高幹爲并州刺史，招以并州左有恒山之險，右有大河之固，帶甲五萬，北阻彊胡，勸幹迎尚，并力觀變。

translations.literal: At that time Shang's cousin by marriage Gao Gan was inspector of Bing Province; Zhao considering that Bing had Mount Heng's peril on the left and the great river's strength on the right fifty thousand armored men and the northern barrier against strong Hu urged Gan to welcome Shang and join forces to watch how matters shifted.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Shang's cousin Gao Gan held Bingzhou; Qian Zhao argued that province flanked Heng Mountain and the Yellow River, fielded fifty thousand men, and blocked the northern tribes—Gao should welcome Yuan Shang and pool strength while watching events.

sentences.zh: 幹旣不能，而陰欲害招。

translations.literal: Gan could not do it yet secretly wished to harm Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Gan refused the advice and secretly plotted against Qian Zhao.

sentences.zh: 招聞之，間行而去，道隔不得追尚，遂東詣太祖。

translations.literal: When Zhao heard this he departed by secret routes; the roads being blocked he could not catch Shang thereupon went east to the Founding Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Qian Zhao slipped away by back roads; blocked from joining Yuan Shang he rode east to Cao Cao.

sentences.zh: 太祖領冀州，辟爲從事。

translations.literal: The Founding Emperor took charge of Ji Province and summoned him as an aide.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao took Ji Province and enlisted him as an aide.

sentences.zh: 太祖將討袁譚，而柳城烏丸欲出騎助譚。

translations.literal: The Founding Emperor was about to attack Yuan Tan but the Wuhuan of Liucheng wished to send cavalry to aid Tan.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao was marching on Yuan Tan while the Liucheng Wuhuan meant to reinforce Tan with horse.

sentences.zh: 太祖以招嘗領烏丸，遣詣柳城。

translations.literal: The Founding Emperor because Zhao had once commanded Wuhuan sent him to Liucheng.
translations.idiomatic: Because Qian Zhao had led Wuhuan troops before Cao Cao dispatched him to Liucheng.

sentences.zh: 到，值峭王嚴，以五千騎當遣詣譚。

translations.literal: When he arrived it happened that King Qiao was strict—he was about to dispatch five thousand riders to Tan.
translations.idiomatic: He arrived as King Qiao stiffened discipline—five thousand riders were ready to ride to Yuan Tan.

sentences.zh: 又遼東太守公孫康自稱平州牧，遣使韓忠齎單于印綬往假峭王。

translations.literal: Moreover Liaodong grand administrator Gongsun Kang styled himself shepherd of Ping Province and sent envoy Han Zhong bearing the seal-cord of the chanyu to confer it on King Qiao.
translations.idiomatic: Liaodong governor Gongsun Kang called himself governor of Ping Province and sent Han Zhong with a chanyu's ribbons to invest King Qiao.

sentences.zh: 峭王大會群長，忠亦在坐。

translations.literal: King Qiao assembled the various chiefs in great convocation; Zhong also sat among them.
translations.idiomatic: King Qiao convened the tribal headmen with Han Zhong in attendance.

sentences.zh: 峭王問招：「昔袁公言受天子之命，假我爲單于；

translations.literal: King Qiao asked Zhao: Formerly Lord Yuan said he received the Son of Heaven's command and provisionally made me chanyu;
translations.idiomatic: King Qiao asked Qian Zhao: 'Yuan Shao once claimed imperial mandate and named me chanyu in his stead;

sentences.zh: 今曹公復言當更白天子，假我真單于；

translations.literal: now Lord Cao again says he must report anew to the Son of Heaven and provisionally make me true chanyu;
translations.idiomatic: Lord Cao now says he will petition the throne again and grant me the genuine title;

sentences.zh: 遼東復持印綬來。

translations.literal: Liaodong again brings seal-cord.
translations.idiomatic: Liaodong has brought another seal and cord.'

sentences.zh: 如此，誰當爲正？

translations.literal: Thus which ought to be authoritative?
translations.idiomatic: Which commission should count?'

sentences.zh: 」招荅曰：「昔袁公承制，得有所拜假；

translations.literal: Zhao replied: Formerly Lord Yuan inherited mandate and could confer provisional appointments;
translations.idiomatic: Qian Zhao answered: 'Yuan Shao ruled under delegated authority and could hand out titles;

sentences.zh: 中間違錯，天子命曹公代之，言當白天子，更假真單于，是也。

translations.literal: in the midst there were violations and errors; the Son of Heaven ordered Lord Cao to replace him—saying one must report to the Son of Heaven and anew confer true chanyu—that is correct.
translations.idiomatic: when that went wrong the emperor invested Cao Cao—who must report south and reissue the true chanyu patent—that order holds.

sentences.zh: 遼東下郡，何得擅稱拜假也？

translations.literal: Liaodong is a subordinate commandery—how can it presumptuously claim to confer appointments?
translations.idiomatic: Liaodong is only a command—how dare it invent appointments on its own?'

sentences.zh: 」忠曰：「我遼東在滄海之東，擁兵百萬，又有扶餘、濊貊之用；

translations.literal: Zhong said: Our Liaodong lies east of the grey sea holds a million troops and moreover has the services of Fuyu and Huimo;
translations.idiomatic: Han Zhong retorted: 'Our Liaodong fronts the sea, commands a vast host, and can call on Fuyu and Huimo;

sentences.zh: 當今之勢，彊者爲右，曹操獨何得爲是也？

translations.literal: in today's situation the strong are honored—how alone can Cao Cao be authoritative?
translations.idiomatic: today the strong rule—why should Cao Cao alone speak for legitimacy?'

sentences.zh: 」招呵忠曰：「曹公允恭明哲，翼戴天子，伐叛柔服，寧靜四海，汝君臣頑嚚，今恃險遠，背違王命，欲擅拜假，侮弄神器，方當屠戮，何敢慢易咎毀大人？

translations.literal: Zhao rebuked Zhong: Lord Cao is sincerely respectful wise and bright—he wings and bears the Son of Heaven punishes rebels and softens those who submit quiets the four seas; your lord and ministers are stubborn and foolish—now relying on distance and peril you violate the king's mandate and wish presumptuously to confer appointments and toy with the sacred vessels—you will soon face slaughter—how dare you slight and slander the great man?
translations.idiomatic: Qian Zhao thundered: 'Cao Cao serves the Han throne—punishing rebels and soothing loyalists across the realm—while your master hides beyond the sea, defies imperial orders, trades counterfeit seals, and mocks the regalia; annihilation awaits you—how dare you insult him?'

sentences.zh: 」便捉忠頭頓築，拔刀欲斬之。

translations.literal: Thereupon he seized Zhong's head and struck it on the ground drew a knife wishing to behead him.
translations.idiomatic: He seized Han Zhong by the hair smashed his face on the floor and drew steel to execute him.

sentences.zh: 峭王驚怖，徒跣抱招，以救請忠，左右失色。

translations.literal: King Qiao was terrified barefoot embraced Zhao pleaded to save Zhong—those left and right lost color.
translations.idiomatic: King Qiao bolted barefoot to clutch Qian Zhao and beg for Han Zhong; every witness went pale.

sentences.zh: 招乃還坐，爲峭王等說成敗之效，禍福所歸，皆下席跪伏，敬受勑教，便辭遼東之使，罷所嚴騎。

translations.literal: Zhao then returned to his seat and for King Qiao and others explained the effects of success and failure and where fortune and disaster lay—they all left their mats knelt prostrate respectfully received instruction then dismissed Liaodong's envoy and stood down the poised riders.
translations.idiomatic: Qian Zhao resumed his seat and lectured the chiefs on profit and ruin until they knelt to obey—then he expelled Liaodong's envoy and canceled the mission to Yuan Tan.

sentences.zh: 太祖滅譚於南皮，署招軍謀掾，從討烏丸。

translations.literal: The Founding Emperor destroyed Tan at Nanpi appointed Zhao army strategic adviser and Zhao accompanied the campaign against Wuhuan.
translations.idiomatic: After Cao Cao crushed Yuan Tan at Nanpi he named Qian Zhao army strategist for the Wuhuan expedition.

sentences.zh: 至柳城，拜護烏丸校尉。

translations.literal: Reaching Liucheng he was appointed colonel protecting Wuhuan.
translations.idiomatic: At Liucheng he received the colonelcy over the Wuhuan.

sentences.zh: 還鄴，遼東送袁尚首，縣在馬市，招覩之悲感，設祭頭下。

translations.literal: Returning to Ye Liaodong sent Yuan Shang's head—it hung in the horse market—Zhao seeing it felt grief and set offerings beneath the head.
translations.idiomatic: Back in Ye Liaodong displayed Yuan Shang's head in the horse market; Qian Zhao wept and sacrificed beneath it.

sentences.zh: 太祖義之，舉爲茂才。

translations.literal: The Founding Emperor deemed him righteous and nominated him flourishing talent.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao praised his loyalty and nominated him flourishing talent.

sentences.zh: 從平漢中，太祖還，留招爲中護軍。

translations.literal: He accompanied the pacification of Hanzhong; the Founding Emperor returned and left Zhao as central protector.
translations.idiomatic: He helped take Hanzhong; Cao Cao then left him as central protector general.

sentences.zh: 事罷，還鄴，拜平虜校尉，將兵督青、徐州郡諸軍事，擊東萊賊，斬其渠率，東土寧靜。

translations.literal: When the affair ended he returned to Ye was appointed colonel who Pacifies Captives led troops supervising military affairs of Qing and Xu provinces attacked bandits of Donglai beheaded their chief and the eastern lands were quiet.
translations.idiomatic: When duty ended he returned to Ye as colonel who Pacifies Captives commanding Qing and Xu forces crushed Donglai bandits and slew their leader—the east grew calm.

sentences.zh: 文帝踐阼，拜招使持節護鮮卑校尉，屯昌平。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen ascended the throne Zhao was appointed bearer of credentials as colonel protecting Xianbei and stationed at Changping.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Pi's accession made Qian Zhao credential-bearing colonel of the Xianbei based at Changping.

sentences.zh: 是時，邊民流散山澤，又亡叛在鮮卑中者，處有千數。

translations.literal: At that time frontier people scattered into mountains and marshes and those who fled or rebelled among the Xianbei numbered in the thousands everywhere.
translations.idiomatic: Frontier folk had fled to hills and swamps while thousands more hid among the Xianbei.

sentences.zh: 招廣布恩信，招誘降附。

translations.literal: Zhao broadly spread kindness and good faith and enticed surrender and attachment.
translations.idiomatic: He broadcast mercy and drew defectors in.

sentences.zh: 建義中郎將公孫集等率將部曲，咸各歸命；

translations.literal: General of the Household who Establishes Righteousness Gongsun Ji and others led their personal followings—all submitted;
translations.idiomatic: Gongsun Ji and other officers marched their private troops to surrender;

sentences.zh: 使還本郡。

translations.literal: he caused them to return to their native commanderies.
translations.idiomatic: he sent them home to their districts.

sentences.zh: 又懷來鮮卑素利、彌加等十餘萬落，皆令款塞。

translations.literal: Moreover he cherished and drew in Suli Mijia and others of the Xianbei—more than one hundred thousand households—all ordered to knock at the barrier.
translations.idiomatic: He also won over Suli Mijia and other Xianbei—over one hundred thousand tents—and brought them to the frontier passes.

sentences.zh: 大軍欲征吳，召招還，至，值軍罷，拜右中郎將，出爲鴈門太守。

translations.literal: The great army wished to campaign against Wu and summoned Zhao back; when he arrived it happened the army was stood down—he was appointed general of the household right and went out as grand administrator of Yanmen.
translations.idiomatic: The court planned war with Wu and recalled him; by the time he arrived the campaign was off—so he became general of the household right and Yanmen governor.

sentences.zh: 郡在邊陲，雖有候望之備，而寇鈔不斷。

translations.literal: The commandery lay on the frontier; though there were lookout preparations raiding did not cease.
translations.idiomatic: Yanmen sat on the edge: guards stood watch yet raids never stopped.

sentences.zh: 招旣教民戰陣，又表復烏丸五百餘家租調，使備鞌馬，遠遣偵候。

translations.literal: Zhao both taught the people battle formations and memorialized to restore rent and tax exemption for more than five hundred Wuhuan households caused them to prepare saddled horses and sent scouts far afield.
translations.idiomatic: He drilled civilians in formation exempted over five hundred Wuhuan households from taxes to equip mounts and pushed scouts deep beyond the wall.

sentences.zh: 虜每犯塞，勒兵逆擊，來輙摧破，於是吏民膽氣日銳，荒野無虞。

translations.literal: Whenever the barbarians violated the barrier he marshaled troops to strike them head-on—each time they came they were shattered—thereupon clerks and people grew daily bolder and the wild wastes were without peril.
translations.idiomatic: Every raid met a counterstroke—nomads broke every time—until officials and farmers grew bold and the steppe grew quiet.

sentences.zh: 又構閒離散，使虜更相猜疑。

translations.literal: Moreover he sowed discord and separation so the barbarians mutually suspected one another.
translations.idiomatic: He also played tribes against one another until mutual suspicion spread.

sentences.zh: 鮮卑大人步度根、泄歸泥等與軻比能爲隙，將部落三萬餘家詣郡附塞。

translations.literal: The Xianbei great men Budugen and Xieguini and others had a rift with Kebineng and led more than thirty thousand households of tribes to the commandery to attach at the barrier.
translations.idiomatic: Chiefs Budugen and Xieguini broke with Kebineng and brought thirty thousand tents to Yanmen's gates.

sentences.zh: 勑令還擊比能，殺比能弟苴羅侯，及叛烏丸歸義侯王同、王寄等，大結怨讎。

translations.literal: He ordered them to return and strike Kebineng—killed Kebineng's younger brother Juluohou and the rebel Wuhuan marquises who Returned to Righteousness Wang Tong Wang Ji and others—greatly forging enmity.
translations.idiomatic: He sent them back against Kebineng killed Kebineng's brother Juluohou and the turncoat Wuhuan nobles Wang Tong and Wang Ji—sparking bitter feud.

sentences.zh: 是以招自出，率將歸泥等討比能於雲中故郡，大破之。

translations.literal: Therefore Zhao himself went out led Xieguini and others to campaign against Kebineng in the old commandery of Yunzhong and smashed him greatly.
translations.idiomatic: Qian Zhao then led Xieguini into old Yunzhong and shattered Kebineng.

sentences.zh: 招通河西鮮卑附頭等十餘萬家，繕治陘北故上館城，置屯戍以鎮內外，夷虜大小莫不歸心，諸亡叛雖親戚不敢藏匿，咸悉收送。

translations.literal: Zhao opened passage to more than one hundred thousand households of Xianbei west of the river including Futou repaired the old Shangguan city north of the pass established garrison colonies to guard inner and outer—Yi and barbarians great and small none failed to submit—all fugitives and rebels even kin dared not harbor them—all were seized and delivered.
translations.idiomatic: He linked over one hundred thousand western Xianbei households led by Futou rebuilt Shanggu city north of the pass garrisoned it inside and out until every tribe acknowledged Han law—fugitives found no shelter even among kin.

sentences.zh: 於是野居晏閉，寇賊靜息。

translations.literal: Thereupon wild dwellings closed peacefully at night and bandits fell silent.
translations.idiomatic: Hamlets barred their gates at dusk and brigandage ceased.

sentences.zh: 招乃簡選有才識者，詣太學受業，還相授教，數年中庠序大興。

translations.literal: Zhao then selected those with talent and knowledge sent them to the academy to study on return they instructed one another—in several years schools flourished greatly.
translations.idiomatic: He picked promising youths for Luoyang's academy who returned as teachers—within years schools flourished.

sentences.zh: 郡所治廣武，井水鹹苦，民皆擔輦遠汲流水，往返七里。

translations.literal: The seat Guangwu—well water was brackish and bitter—the people all carried poles and carts to draw flowing water far away seven li round trip.
translations.idiomatic: Guangwu's wells ran salt and foul so families hauled sweet water seven li round trip.

sentences.zh: 招準望地勢，因山陵之宜，鑿原開渠，注水城內，民賴其益。

translations.literal: Zhao surveyed terrain according to the lay of hills and opened channels from high ground led water inside the city—the people relied on the benefit.
translations.idiomatic: He read the hills cut channels from high ground and fed fresh water into the walls.

sentences.zh: 招子嘉嗣。

translations.literal: Zhao's son Jia succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Qian Jia inherited the title.

sentences.zh: 次子弘，亦猛毅有招風，以隴西太守隨鄧艾伐蜀有功，咸熈中爲振威護軍。

translations.literal: The second son Hong was also fierce and resolute with Zhao's manner—as grand administrator of Longxi he followed Deng Ai to attack Shu with merit—in the Xianxi era became protector general who Inspires Might.
translations.idiomatic: Second son Hong matched his father's grit as Longxi governor he earned laurels under Deng Ai against Shu and became protector Inspires Might under Jin.

sentences.zh: 嘉與晉司徒李胤同母，早卒。

translations.literal: Jia shared a mother with Jin minister of education Li Yin and died young.
translations.idiomatic: Qian Jia was Li Yin's half-brother and died young.

sentences.zh: 〈案《晉書》：弘後爲揚州、涼州刺史，以果烈死事於邊。

translations.literal: According to the Jin shu Hong later became inspector of Yangzhou and Liangzhou and died in frontier service owing to resolute valor.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin history adds that Hong later governed Yangzhou and Liangzhou and fell on the frontier proving his courage.

sentences.zh: 嘉子秀，字成叔。

translations.literal: Jia's son Xiu courtesy name Chengshu.
translations.idiomatic: Qian Jia's son Qian Xiu courtesy Chengshu.

sentences.zh: 荀綽《冀州記》曰：秀有儁才，性豪俠有氣，弱冠得美名。

translations.literal: Xun Chuo's Ji Province record says Xiu had outstanding talent nature heroic and generous with spirit—in weak cap he gained fair renown.
translations.idiomatic: Xun Chuo's Ji Province gazetteer praises Xiu's genius brash heroism and early fame.

sentences.zh: 於太康中爲衞瓘、崔洪、石崇等所提攜，以新安令博士爲司空從事中郎。

translations.literal: In the Taikang era he was promoted by Wei Guan Cui Hong Shi Chong and others—from magistrate of Xin'an and erudite became aide-de-camp to the minister of works.
translations.idiomatic: Under Taikang Wei Guan Cui Hong and Shi Chong pulled him from Xin'an magistrate and doctorate to aide in the ministry of works.

sentences.zh: 與帝舅黃門侍郎王愷素相輕侮。

translations.literal: With the emperor's uncle attendant at the yellow gates Wang Kai he long mutually despised and insulted.
translations.idiomatic: He traded insults for years with Wang Kai the emperor's uncle at the yellow gates.

sentences.zh: 愷諷司隷荀愷，令都官誣奏秀夜在道中載高平國守士田興妻。

translations.literal: Kai hinted to metropolitan commander Xun Kai and ordered the capital officials falsely memorialize that Xiu by night on the road carried off the wife of frontier soldier Tian Xing of Gaoping principality.
translations.idiomatic: Kai nudged metropolitan commander Xun Kai to charge Qian Xiu with abducting Tian Xing's wife from Gaoping on the road at night.

sentences.zh: 秀即表訴被誣陷之由，論愷穢行，文辭尤厲。

translations.literal: Xiu immediately memorialized explaining the reason he was framed and discussed Kai's foul conduct—the wording especially harsh.
translations.idiomatic: Qian Xiu fired back a memorial exposing the frame-up and Kai's filth in blistering prose.

sentences.zh: 于時朝臣雖多證明，秀名譽由是而損。

translations.literal: Though many court ministers then bore witness for him Xiu's reputation suffered from this.
translations.idiomatic: Many ministers defended him yet his name never recovered.

sentences.zh: 後張華請爲長史，稍遷至尚書。

translations.literal: Later Zhang Hua requested him as chief clerk—gradually promoted to secretary.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Hua later employed him as chief clerk until he rose to secretary.

sentences.zh: 河間王以秀爲平北將軍，假節，在馮翊遇害。

translations.literal: The prince of Hejian appointed Xiu general who Pacifies the North granted credentials—he met death at Fengyi.
translations.idiomatic: The prince of Hejian named him Pacifies-the-North general with staff—he died at Fengyi.

sentences.zh: 世人玩其辭賦，惜其材幹。〉

translations.literal: Men of the age admired his rhapsodies and regretted his talents.
translations.idiomatic: Later readers savor his verse and mourn the waste of his gifts.

sentences.zh: 郭淮字伯濟，太原陽曲人也。

translations.literal: Guo Huai's courtesy name was Boji; he was a man of Yangqu in Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Huai courtesy Boji was a native of Yangqu in Taiyuan.
