sentences.zh: 〈案

translations.literal: Investigation marker opening Pei Songzhi's note.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Songzhi opens an annotation with

sentences.zh: 〈郭氏譜〉

translations.literal: Title line Genealogy of the Guo clan.
translations.idiomatic: the heading Genealogy of the Guo lineage.

sentences.zh: ：淮祖全，大司農；

translations.literal: Colon introducing pedigree Huai's grandfather Quan was minister of agriculture;
translations.idiomatic: It records that Guo Huai's grandfather Guo Quan served as minister of agriculture;

sentences.zh: 父縕，鴈門太守。〉

translations.literal: his father Yun was grand administrator of Yanmen closing the citation.
translations.idiomatic: his father Guo Yun governed Yanmen.

sentences.zh: 建安中舉孝廉，除平原府丞。

translations.literal: In the Jian'an era he was recommended filial and incorrupt and appointed assistant to the governor of Pingyuan.
translations.idiomatic: He earned recommendation as filial and incorrupt during Jian'an and became assistant to the Pingyuan governor.

sentences.zh: 文帝爲五官將，召淮署爲門下賊曹，轉爲丞相兵曹議令史，從征漢中。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen was general of the five offices he summoned Huai to serve as clerk for bandits under his gate transferred to clerk for deliberations in the chancellor's bureau of military affairs accompanied the Hanzhong expedition.
translations.idiomatic: While crown prince Cao Pi enlisted him as gatehouse clerk for bandits then as military-affairs clerk under the chancellor and took him on the Hanzhong campaign.

sentences.zh: 太祖還，留征西將軍夏侯淵拒劉備，以淮爲淵司馬。

translations.literal: The Founding Emperor returned and left west-conquering general Xiahou Yuan to oppose Liu Bei appointing Huai as Yuan's major.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao left Xiahou Yuan to face Liu Bei and made Guo Huai Yuan's major.

sentences.zh: 淵與備戰，淮時有疾不出。

translations.literal: Yuan battled Bei; Huai at the time was ill and did not go out.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Huai stayed behind sick when Yuan fought Liu Bei.

sentences.zh: 淵遇害，軍中擾擾，淮收散卒，推盪寇將軍張郃爲軍主，諸營乃定。

translations.literal: When Yuan met harm the army was in turmoil; Huai gathered scattered troops promoted campaign-general Zhang He as army commander—then the camps stabilized.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuan fell the army panicked; Guo Huai rallied the fugitives and pushed Zhang He to command until order returned.

sentences.zh: 其明日，備欲渡漢水來攻。

translations.literal: The next day Bei wished to cross the Han River to attack.
translations.idiomatic: Next day Liu Bei meant to ford the Han and strike.

sentences.zh: 諸將議衆寡不敵，備便乘勝，欲依水爲陣以拒之。

translations.literal: The generals debated that numbers did not match and Bei would ride victory—they wished to array along the water to resist him.
translations.idiomatic: His officers feared Liu Bei's momentum and wanted to fight along the bank.

sentences.zh: 淮曰：「此示弱而不足挫敵，非筭也。

translations.literal: Huai said: This shows weakness yet is insufficient to blunt the enemy—it is not sound calculation.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Huai objected: lining the bank advertises weakness without stopping Liu Bei.

sentences.zh: 不如遠水爲陣，引而致之，半濟而後擊，備可破也。

translations.literal: Better array far from the water lure and draw him—strike after half have crossed—and Bei can be broken.
translations.idiomatic: Stand back from the river lure him halfway across then hit him—that breaks Liu Bei.

sentences.zh: 」旣陣，備疑不渡，淮遂堅守，示無還心。

translations.literal: Once arrayed Bei hesitated and did not cross; Huai therefore held firm showing no intent to withdraw.
translations.idiomatic: They deployed; Liu Bei stalled at the ford while Guo Huai dug in showing no retreat.

sentences.zh: 以狀聞，太祖善之，假郃節，復以淮爲司馬。

translations.literal: He reported the situation— the Founding Emperor approved granted He credentials again made Huai major.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao approved gave Zhang He the staff and kept Guo Huai as major.

sentences.zh: 文帝即王位，賜爵關內侯，轉爲鎮西長史。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen assumed the kingly rank Huai was gifted secondary marquis within the passes and transferred to chief clerk who Guards the West.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Pi's kingship brought Guo Huai a secondary marquisate and the western headquarters chief clerk post.

sentences.zh: 又行征羌護軍，護左將軍張郃、冠軍將軍楊秋討山賊鄭甘、盧水叛胡，皆破平之。

translations.literal: Also acted protector general who Conquers the Qiang supervising general of the left Zhang He and champion general Yang Qiu to attack mountain bandit Zheng Gan and rebel Hu of Lushui—all defeated and pacified.
translations.idiomatic: He also led the Qiang-conquest guards with Zhang He and Yang Qiu against Zheng Gan's hill bandits and Lushui rebels until both were crushed.

sentences.zh: 關中始定，民得安業。

translations.literal: Guanzhong began to settle and the people could pursue peaceful occupations.
translations.idiomatic: The Guanzhong plain steadied and farmers returned to their fields.

sentences.zh: 黃初元年，奉使賀文帝踐阼，而道路得疾，故計遠近爲稽留。

translations.literal: In the first year of Huangchu he was dispatched on mission to congratulate Emperor Wen's accession but on the road fell ill—therefore calculating distance was delayed.
translations.idiomatic: Huangchu 1: sent to greet Cao Pi's enthronement he fell ill en route and arrived late.

sentences.zh: 及群臣歡會，帝正色責之曰：「昔禹會諸侯於塗山，防風後至，便行大戮。

translations.literal: When the hosts of ministers feasted together the emperor with stern countenance rebuked him saying: Formerly Yu assembled the feudal lords at Mount Tu—Fangfeng arrived late and was forthwith greatly executed.
translations.idiomatic: At court feast Cao Pi rebuked him: Yu assembled lords at Tu Mountain and executed late Fangfeng.

sentences.zh: 今溥天同慶而卿最留遲，何也？

translations.literal: Now all under heaven rejoices alike yet you are the most delayed—why?
translations.idiomatic: All the realm celebrates yet you lag worst—why?

sentences.zh: 」淮對曰：「臣聞五帝先教導民以德，夏后政衰，始用刑辟。

translations.literal: Huai replied: Your servant has heard the Five Emperors first instructed the people with virtue; when the Xia lord's government declined they began to use punishments.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Huai answered: The Five Emperors ruled through virtue; harsh law began only when Xia declined.

sentences.zh: 今臣遭唐虞之世，是以自知免於防風之誅也。

translations.literal: Now your servant encounters an age like Tang and Yu—therefore I know myself spared Fangfeng's execution.
translations.idiomatic: I live under a sage-king like Yao and Shun—so I escape Fangfeng's fate.

sentences.zh: 」帝恱之，擢領雍州刺史，封射陽亭侯，五年爲真。

translations.literal: The emperor was pleased promoted him to concurrent inspector of Yong Province enfeoffed him village marquis of Sheyang—in the fifth year the post became substantive.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor laughed promoted him acting Yongzhou inspector and village marquis of Sheyang—full appointment came in year five.

sentences.zh: 安定羗大帥辟蹏反，討破降之。

translations.literal: The great Qiang chief of Anding Piti rebelled—Huai campaigned defeated him and accepted his surrender.
translations.idiomatic: When Anding Qiang chief Piti rose Guo Huai crushed him and took his surrender.

sentences.zh: 每羌、胡來降，淮輙先使人推問其親理，男女多少，年歲長幼；

translations.literal: Whenever Qiang or Hu came to surrender Huai always first sent men to inquire into their kin relations how many men and women ages young and old;
translations.idiomatic: Whenever Qiang or Hu defectors arrived Guo Huai first tallied kin counts ages and sexes;

sentences.zh: 及見，一二知其款曲，訊問周至，咸稱神明。

translations.literal: When he saw them from one or two matters he grasped their inner wishes; interrogation was exhaustive—all praised him as godlike.
translations.idiomatic: At interview he read each party after a detail or two questioned thoroughly and earned a reputation for uncanny judgment.

sentences.zh: 太和二年，蜀相諸葛亮出祁山，遣將軍馬謖至街亭，高詳屯列柳城。

translations.literal: In the second year of Taihe Shu chancellor Zhuge Liang issued from Qishan; he dispatched general Ma Su to Jieting while Gao Xiang encamped at Liuliu fort.
translations.idiomatic: Taihe 2: Zhuge Liang drove out of Qishan Ma Su toward Jieting and Gao Xiang toward Liuliu.

sentences.zh: 張郃擊謖，淮攻詳營，皆破之。

translations.literal: Zhang He struck Su; Huai attacked Xiang's camp—both were shattered.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang He routed Ma Su while Guo Huai stormed Gao Xiang's camp—both Shu forces broke.

sentences.zh: 又破隴西名羌唐蹏於枹罕，加建威將軍。

translations.literal: Moreover he defeated the famed Longxi Qiang Tangti at Fuhan and was advanced general who Establishes Might.
translations.idiomatic: He also crushed the prominent Longxi Qiang Tangti near Fuhan and took rank as Establishes Might general.

sentences.zh: 五年，蜀出鹵城。

translations.literal: In the fifth year Shu issued from Lucheng.
translations.idiomatic: Year five saw another Shu thrust out of Lucheng.

sentences.zh: 是時，隴右無穀，議欲關中大運，淮以威恩撫循羌、胡，家使出穀，平其輸調，軍食用足，轉揚武將軍。

translations.literal: At that time Longyou lacked grain; deliberation wished for grand transport from Guanzhong—Huai by awe and kindness soothed Qiang and Hu caused each household to yield grain equalized their levies and grain for the army became sufficient—he was transferred general who Displays Martial Might.
translations.idiomatic: Longyou wanted grain and debate favored hauling from Guanzhong; Guo Huai soothed tribes with blended awe and mercy until households tithed grain fair levies fed the army and he rose to Displays Martial Might general.

sentences.zh: 青龍二年，諸葛亮出斜谷，並田于蘭坑。

translations.literal: In the second year of Qinglong Zhuge Liang issued from Xie Valley and practiced parallel farming at Rank Hollow.
translations.idiomatic: Qinglong 2: Zhuge Liang emerged from Xie Valley and opened cooperative farms at Rank Hollow.

sentences.zh: 是時司馬宣王屯渭南；

translations.literal: At that time Sima Yi was stationed south of the Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Yi held the south bank of the Wei.

sentences.zh: 淮策亮必爭北原，宜先據之，議者多謂不然。

translations.literal: Huai calculated Liang would surely contest the northern plain—it was fitting first to seize it—many debaters said not so.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Huai insisted Zhuge Liang would fight for the northern plateau and wanted to seize it first—most advisers disagreed.

sentences.zh: 淮曰：「若亮跨渭登原，連兵北山，隔絕隴道，搖盪民、夷，此非國之利也。

translations.literal: Huai said: If Liang spans the Wei and mounts the plateau links troops on the northern hills and cuts the Long road swaying people and Yi—this is not to the state's advantage.
translations.idiomatic: He warned: if Zhuge Liang crosses the Wei gains the heights links to the northern hills and severs Longzhou road he will sway Han Chinese and tribes alike—that hurts Wei.

sentences.zh: 」宣王善之，淮遂屯北原。

translations.literal: Yi approved it; Huai therefore encamped on the northern plain.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Yi agreed so Guo Huai seized the northern plateau.

sentences.zh: 塹壘未成，蜀兵大至，淮逆擊之。

translations.literal: Trenches and ramparts not yet finished Shu troops arrived in force; Huai struck them head-on.
translations.idiomatic: Before the ditch works finished Shu attacked in strength; Guo Huai counterattacked.

sentences.zh: 後數日，亮盛兵西行，諸將皆謂欲攻西圍，淮獨以爲此見形於西，欲使官兵重應之，必攻陽遂耳。

translations.literal: Several days later Liang displayed troops marching west; the generals all said he intended to assault the western siege lines—Huai alone thought this showed form in the west intending to make government troops heavily respond there—he would surely attack Yangsui.
translations.idiomatic: Days later Zhuge Liang feinted west; officers assumed a strike on the western perimeter—Guo Huai alone read it as a feint to draw Wei west while the real blow would hit Yangsui.

sentences.zh: 其夜果攻陽遂，有備不得上。

translations.literal: That night they indeed attacked Yangsui—there was preparation and they could not ascend.
translations.idiomatic: That night Shu struck Yangsui but the garrison held and they failed to scale the walls.

sentences.zh: 正始元年，蜀將羌維出隴西。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhengshi Shu general Jiang Wei issued from Longxi.
translations.idiomatic: Zhengshi 1: Jiang Wei of Shu drove out of Longxi.

sentences.zh: 淮遂進軍，追至彊中，維退，遂討羌迷當等，案撫柔氐三千餘落，拔徙以實關中。

translations.literal: Huai therefore advanced the army pursued to Qiangzhong Wei withdrew then campaigned against Qiang Midang and others investigated soothed and softened more than three thousand households of Di uprooted them moved them to settle Guanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Huai pushed to Qiangzhong Jiang Wei pulled back then he attacked Qiang chief Midang pacified over three thousand Di households and relocated them to thicken Guanzhong settlement.

sentences.zh: 遷左將軍。

translations.literal: He was promoted general of the left.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to general of the left.

sentences.zh: 涼州休屠胡梁元碧等，率種落二千餘家附雍州。

translations.literal: Xutu Hu of Liangzhou Liang Yuanbi and others led more than two thousand households of their tribes to attach to Yong Province.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yuanbi and Xutu Hu bands from Liangzhou brought over two thousand tents to Yongzhou's allegiance.

sentences.zh: 淮奏請使居安定之高平，爲民保鄣，其後因置西川都尉。

translations.literal: Huai memorialized requesting to cause them dwell at Gaoping in Anding as bulwark for the people—afterward accordingly established westriver commandant.
translations.idiomatic: He asked to settle them at Gaoping in Anding as a shield for civilians—later the westriver commandant post followed.

sentences.zh: 轉拜前將軍，領州如故。

translations.literal: He was transferred appointment general of the van concurrently administering the province as before.
translations.idiomatic: He turned general of the van while still governing the province.

sentences.zh: 五年，夏侯玄伐蜀，淮督諸軍爲前鋒。

translations.literal: In the fifth year Xiahou Xuan campaigned against Shu; Huai supervised various armies as van.
translations.idiomatic: Year five Xiahou Xuan invaded Shu with Guo Huai commanding the van.

sentences.zh: 淮度勢不利，輙拔軍出，故不大敗。

translations.literal: Huai gauged the situation disadvantageous forthwith withdrew the army therefore did not greatly lose.
translations.idiomatic: Reading disaster in the odds Guo Huai pulled out early and avoided a rout.

sentences.zh: 還假淮節。

translations.literal: On return Huai was lent credentials.
translations.idiomatic: On withdrawal he received the credential staff.

sentences.zh: 八年，隴西、南安、金城、西平諸羌餓何、燒戈、伐同、蛾遮塞等相結叛亂，攻圍城邑，南招蜀兵，涼州名胡治無戴復叛應之。

translations.literal: In the eighth year various Qiang of Longxi Nan'an Jinxi Xiping—E He Shaoge Fatong Ezhesai et al.—linked in rebellion besieged towns summoned Shu troops southward and famed Hu of Liangzhou Zhi Wudai again rebelled in response.
translations.idiomatic: Year eight Longxi Nan'an Jinxi and Xiping Qiang—E He Shaoge Fatong Ezhesai—combined besieged cities called Shu south while Liangzhou's Zhi Wudai rebelled again to join them.

sentences.zh: 討蜀護軍夏侯霸督諸軍屯爲翅。

translations.literal: Shu protector general Xiahou Ba supervised various armies encamped at Weichi.
translations.idiomatic: Xiahou Ba Shu-conquest protector camped the host at Weichi.

sentences.zh: 淮軍始到狄道，議者僉謂宜先討定枹罕，內平惡羌，外折賊謀。

translations.literal: When Huai's army first reached Didao debaters unanimously said one ought first attack pacify Fuhan pacify wicked Qiang within break enemy plotting without.
translations.idiomatic: At Didao every adviser urged clearing Fuhan first to crush hostile Qiang inside and spoil Shu designs outside.

sentences.zh: 淮策維必來攻霸，遂入渢中，轉南迎霸。

translations.literal: Huai calculated Wei would surely come attack Ba therefore entered Fengzhong turned south to meet Ba.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Huai bet Jiang Wei would strike Xiahou Ba so he slipped into Fengzhong and swung south to reinforce Ba.

sentences.zh: 維果攻爲翅，會淮軍適至，維遁退。

translations.literal: Wei indeed attacked Weichi—it happened Huai's army arrived just then Wei fled.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Wei did hit Weichi just as Guo Huai arrived—Wei withdrew.

sentences.zh: 進討叛羌，斬餓何、燒戈，降服者萬餘落。

translations.literal: Advancing to punish rebel Qiang he beheaded E He and Shaoge—those who submitted numbered more than ten thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: He marched against the rebels slew E He and Shaoge and enrolled over ten thousand tents.

sentences.zh: 九年，遮塞等屯河關、白土故城，據河拒軍。

translations.literal: In the ninth year Zhesai and others encamped at Heguan and Bai tu old city holding the river to oppose the army.
translations.idiomatic: Year nine Zhesai held Heguan and old Bai tu astride the river to block Wei.

sentences.zh: 淮見形上流，密於下渡兵據白土城，擊，大破之。

translations.literal: Huai displayed form upstream secretly at the lower ford crossed troops seized Bai tu city struck greatly shattered them.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Huai feigned upstream movement slipped troops across downstream seized Bai tu city and smashed them.

sentences.zh: 治無戴圍武威，家屬留在西海。

translations.literal: Zhi Wudai besieged Wuwei while family dependents remained at Xihai.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi Wudai invested Wuwei while kin stayed at Lake Xihai.

sentences.zh: 淮進軍趨西海，欲掩取其累重，會無戴折還，與戰於龍夷之北，破走之。

translations.literal: Huai advanced the army hastened Xihai intending to surprise seize their baggage—it happened Wudai doubled back battled north of Longyi defeated and drove him.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Huai raced toward Xihai to loot trains—Zhi Wudai doubled back met him north of Longyi and fled broken.

sentences.zh: 令居惡虜在石頭山之西，當大道止，斷絕王使。

translations.literal: The wicked barbarians of Lingju west of Stone Mountain stood athwart the great road cutting off royal envoys.
translations.idiomatic: Hostile tribes west of Stone Mountain at Lingju blocked the highway and seized imperial couriers.

sentences.zh: 淮還過討，大破之。

translations.literal: Huai on return passed through campaigned against greatly shattered them.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Huai smashed them on the march home.

sentences.zh: 姜維出石營，從彊川，乃西迎治無戴，留陰平太守廖化於成重山築城，斂破羌保質。

translations.literal: Jiang Wei emerged Shiying followed Qiangchuan went west to meet Zhi Wudai left Yinping prefect Liao Hua building a fort at Chengzhong Mountain collecting Poqiang hostages.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Wei sortied from Shiying up Qiangchuan west to link Zhi Wudai while prefect Liao Hua walled Chengzhong Mountain and rounded Poqiang hostages.

sentences.zh: 淮欲分兵取之。

translations.literal: Huai wished to divide troops to take him.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Huai meant to split forces and seize one wing.

sentences.zh: 諸將以維衆西接彊胡，化以據險，分軍兩持，兵勢轉弱，進不制維，退不拔化，非計也，不如合而俱西，及胡、蜀未接，絕其內外，此伐交之兵也。

translations.literal: The generals considered Wei's host west joins strong Hu Hua holding peril dividing the army two fronts military momentum turns weak advancing cannot control Wei retreating cannot uproot Hua—it is not a plan—better unite and go west together while Hu and Shu have not linked sever them inner and outer—this is troop that cuts alliances.
translations.idiomatic: His officers argued Jiang Wei touches powerful tribes west while Liao Hua holds rugged ground splitting the army weakens both prongs—neither nails Jiang Wei nor takes Liao Hua better march west in one body before Shu links with the tribes sever inside from outside Sunzi's diplomacy stroke.

sentences.zh: 淮曰：「今往取化，出賊不意，維必狼顧。

translations.literal: Huai said: Now going to seize Hua catches the bandits unaware Wei must look anxiously backward.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Huai countered: Hit Liao Hua first catch Shu off guard Jiang Wei will whirl about.

sentences.zh: 比維自致，足以定化，且使維疲於奔命。

translations.literal: By the time Wei arrives of himself it suffices to settle Hua and moreover causes Wei to weary running on errands.
translations.idiomatic: When Jiang Wei doubles back we can finish Liao Hua and leave Jiang Wei exhausted.

sentences.zh: 兵不遠西，而胡交自離，此一舉而兩全之策也。

translations.literal: Troops need not go far west yet Hu alliances separate of themselves—this is one stroke completing two policies.
translations.idiomatic: No distant western march yet tribal allies peel away—one blow two gains.

sentences.zh: 」乃別遣夏侯霸等追維於沓中，淮自率諸軍就攻化等。

translations.literal: Thereupon separately dispatched Xiahou Ba and others to pursue Wei in Taozhong Huai himself led various armies to attack Hua and companions.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Xiahou Ba after Jiang Wei in Taozhong while Guo Huai personally assaulted Liao Hua.

sentences.zh: 維果馳還救化，皆如淮計。

translations.literal: Wei indeed galloped back to rescue Hua—all accorded with Huai's calculation.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Wei raced back to save Liao Hua exactly as Guo Huai predicted.

sentences.zh: 進封都鄉侯。

translations.literal: Advanced enfeoffment village marquis of Du.
translations.idiomatic: His fief advanced to village marquis of Du township.

translations.literal: Bracket heading Evaluation.
translations.idiomatic: Section heading Historical appraisal.

sentences.zh: 評曰：滿寵立志剛毅，勇而有謀。

translations.literal: The appraisal states: Man Chong set his resolve firm and austere—courageous yet possessing stratagem.
translations.idiomatic: Appraisal: Man Chong was stern resolute brave and resourceful.

sentences.zh: 田豫居身清白，規畧明練。

translations.literal: Tian Yu kept himself pure and white—plans and overview bright and practiced.
translations.idiomatic: Tian Yu lived incorruptibly and planned with lucid skill.

sentences.zh: 牽招秉義壯烈，威績顯著。

translations.literal: Qian Zhao grasped righteousness fierce and martyr-like—awe-inspiring deeds conspicuous.
translations.idiomatic: Qian Zhao upheld duty with fiery valor and striking achievement.

sentences.zh: 郭淮方策精詳，垂問秦、雍。

translations.literal: Guo Huai's strategies were refined and thorough—his counsel extended through Qin and Yong.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Huai engineered meticulous campaigns and framed frontier policy for Qinzhou and Yongzhou.

sentences.zh: 而豫位止小州，招終於郡守，未盡其用也。

translations.literal: Yet Yu's rank stopped at a minor province Zhao ended as grand administrator—they did not exhaust their usefulness.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Tian Yu never rose beyond a small province and Qian Zhao died a mere governor—their talents were never fully spent.
